schedule.strategy: A worker with zero Census ends after its prelude; otherwise all units in its clipped interval are visited, including masked no-payload units. Assigned completion includes any elected finalization and scratch reset. Clamp data is read only when the nullable input is present.

For an immediate request the host writes -1 to the pinned mirror before submitting this graph and uses the bounded polling/final-read rule in when to submit the full graph. A timeout neither cancels this work nor supplies a completion event. For a captured outer request, the host sentinel write occurs at recording only; execution follows the recorded two-graph sequence without polling or a fresh host sentinel write. The first mirror is not consumed by any full-graph guard. Host return does not wait for final output completion. Cached state has same-stream ordering but no added cross-stream exclusion.

A worker with zero Census ends after its prelude; otherwise all units in its clipped interval are visited, including masked no-payload units. Assigned completion includes any elected finalization and scratch reset. Clamp data is read only when the nullable input is present.

Before the probe, contiguous Contract inputs need no copies. The rebuild's
route_hist reads route_ids to the host at most once, counts valid IDs and
caches that statistic only for this rebuild's default selection gates.
ensure_tables is already satisfied. Allocate a fresh four-byte ProbeDirty
and submit its zero fill on the caller stream before the scan.
After scan submission, the helper checks the launch status. On success it
attempts a caller-stream synchronization; only if that succeeds does it
attempt a four-byte device-to-host copy into a host integer initialized to 1.
It frees the temporary on every post-submission exit. Launch/synchronization
errors return -3/-4; the copy status is unchecked. Python accepts only return 1,
and exceptions retain zero_ok=false. An error is not a completion guarantee.
The device stream still orders the recorded scan before the main launch.
After the helper returns, workspace lookup either reuses matching backing
storage or allocates it and zero-initializes the 2*E Counts/Fill allocation.
Preparation overwrites all Counts; Fill is unused by this small-route path.
Other allocations retain unspecified bytes; no initialization of the partial
or expert-ID tails is inferred. No zflag or pinned verification mirror is allocated.
Tensor-map construction and ABI publication do not execute the expert computation.
The five-kernel chain is submitted once, eagerly or by graph replay; successful
private-stream capture records it without executing a second copy. After a zero
moe_run status, the published ABI retains its tensor and workspace owners.
The prefix's copies, fills and allocation services are preserved here without
inventing implementation-specific computational kernels for those APIs.
There is no host synchronization of the main chain added by this design.
The source's concurrent verdict stores and unchecked readback do not establish a reliable probe result on error; zero_ok=false retains the complete main chain.

mapping.strategy: Before the probe, Model.forward's calling host executes host_selection after one ordered route-ID readback through ids.tolist(). Its histogram is reused by the default WS and nonempty-route gates in this rebuild and discarded afterwards. In this low-R cfg81 domain the WS gate uses HostTiles; the saved small threshold is 6500. These host choices do not supply device route maps. Only the predicate scan runs on the workers below; its result is consumed by the host, not by verify.

Member v in [0,VerifyCTAs) visits flattened chunks [256*v+256*VerifyCTAs*l,256*v+256*VerifyCTAs*l+256), clipped to each traversal extent, for l>=0. Output chunks count eight BF16 elements, payload chunks count four bytes, and scale, score and parameter chunks count one element. These traversals are separate local loops, not a Cartesian product. The optional limit is traversed only when present; every member participates in the final reduction even with an empty traversal.

verb.prepare: First issue the assigned route-less rows' vector zero stores. All threads independently test each such token's route IDs. Then scan all R IDs with disjoint thread strides, reduce to sixteen warp totals in Exchange, rendezvous the CTA, let one thread sum those totals into Census, and rendezvous again. Done publishes Census locally; kernel completion covers the output stores. No payload, weights, counters or route accumulators are touched when Census=0.

verb.inspect: Unit(v) resolves the statically assigned u(v), route, intermediate chunk and current expert ID. Define ValidUnit(v)=1 for an in-range expert and 0 otherwise. Invalid units have no following payload or synchronization actions. The cached token identity starts invalid and changes only on a valid unit's input preparation.
verb.prepare: If this valid unit changes the cached token, decode its entire X from global packed input and scales through the already initialized global E2M1/E4M3 lookup tables, and have one thread count its valid routes into TokenCount. Retain X and TokenCount while the token is unchanged. InputCache includes H/8 unused padding elements. Complete a CTA rendezvous on every valid unit, including a cache hit. Any previous token's input reads finished before this slot can change.
verb.contract: Execute fc1 using all sixteen warps, with two up/gate pairs per warp and the 32 reduction groups mapped across its lanes. Weight payloads and scales are read directly from global memory through the format tables; no shared weight buffer is allocated. Group starts at zero for this unit. After its local reduction, publish UpGate to shared memory and rendezvous all warps before activation.
verb.quantize: Warp zero consumes UpGate, evaluates activate and forms the two independent 16-channel maxima. It publishes the B FP32 QChunk values, then all sixteen warps rendezvous. UpGate is now consumed; QChunk remains live until every FC2 hidden stripe has read it.
verb.accumulate: Each thread computes four consecutive hidden channels at a time, traversing the next stripe after 2048 channels. Read each unit's packed FC2 weight slice and scales directly from global memory, consume QChunk, and issue scalar FP32 atomic additions of Partial into RouteAccum. All H channels are covered. Done means this CTA's additions have been issued and QChunk's local reads have ended; publication to other CTAs is completed by arrive.
verb.arrive: Every thread publishes its own RouteAccum additions to device scope, then the CTA rendezvous orders those publications before one elected thread increments Arrivals[t]. Record Last=1 exactly for the ticket n(t)*S-1 and 0 otherwise; publish it to all threads with a CTA rendezvous. The last-arrival consumption ordering makes all n(t)*S units' contributions visible before final reads. This protocol does not wait for other CTAs to reach a grid barrier. Last(v,a) names this unit's returned flag for the nested occurrence a.
verb.gather: Only the last unit executes this action. One thread collects valid flattened route indices into prelude's Exchange.FinalRoutes and their current routing weights into FinalScores in increasing slot order. The census already consumed Exchange.WarpCounts. Rendezvous before any thread reads the finalizer metadata.
verb.finalize: Execute fc2_finalize in four-hidden-element stripes: initialize the current stripe of Z in OutputSum, read the completed route sums, cast each route value to BF16 before its weighted FP32 FMA, reset each consumed route accumulator stripe, and write the BF16 output stripe. Finish the CTA's output and reset store submissions, rendezvous, then one thread resets Arrivals[t]. No output scratch array is created. Global completion and visibility to later requests are supplied by the single kernel's completion.
verb.advance: Rendezvous all sixteen warps after every valid unit, including a non-last unit that did no finalization. This protects Last, TokenCount, UpGate, QChunk and finalizer metadata before subsequent units reuse them. The elected finalizer has submitted its counter reset before this rendezvous completes; no per-unit global wait or grid synchronization is inserted.

verb.enter: All threads wait for predecessor completion and visibility; warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. This trigger does not publish the verdict or output.
verb.produce: Stream the shard's FirstZeroOutput region with 16-byte zero stores, covering all caller output elements exactly once across shards. Stores may remain in flight until kernel completion.
verb.compute:
Keep one Predicate accumulator per thread across the separate payload,
activation-scale, route-weight and parameter scans. Start each at zero,
OR its dirty tests, then perform a CTA-wide OR rendezvous to obtain Dirty(0,b).
The optional clamp input is accessed only when enabled.
verb.fold:
One thread contributes Dirty(0,b) to the global dirty-OR word when nonzero,
orders that contribution before its atomic arrival ticket with a device
fence, and takes one ticket. The last arrival reads the combined dirty
word, writes FirstClean, and resets the dirty word and arrival counter to zero.
Other arrivals perform no verdict store. The pinned mirror is nonzero, so
the winner executes a system fence then a volatile store of the same
verdict. Done means this shard's contribution and any winner tail are
finished; it does not imply that other shards' output stores have drained.
Only verify_first.kernel_done makes the complete FirstZeroOutput and FirstClean available
before the second verifier reuses their storage. State reuse follows same-stream execution ordering,
not the early trigger or the host-mirror store.

The last stage also commits result readiness for the epilogue. Same-issuer ordering ensures an earlier MMA has consumed ScaleTM before a later scale copy overwrites that scale slot, and makes each scale copy visible before the MMA that uses it.

resolve.meaning: Resolve the expert and compact row base. Populate RowIndex for all BM rows, redirecting padding rows to base(j), then rendezvous the CTA. Both ActQ payload and ActS scale loads use this map throughout the worktile.

scale.meaning: ScalePair(t,k) loads one 16-byte ActS row and four prepared 4-byte weight-scale words per operand row, then stores their complete AScale and BScale images in slot k modulo three. Preserve the prepared scale permutation and establish shared-to-async visibility. Done includes these synchronous loads, shared stores and the proxy fence; acquire supplies CTA-wide publication. No scale-prefetch buffer survives this action. The first two valid stages are primed; later scales are refilled after the MMA two stages earlier is issued, allowing the scale-load latency to overlap that MMA.

verb.stage: CopyGroup(t,s) submits 16-byte asynchronous copies for the complete PayloadA and PayloadB images of stage s into slot s modulo three, and commits one group. Use RowIndex for ActQ and the prepared weight-row mapping for gemm2_weights. Done covers the payload copies, before acquire's CTA publication. For s >= I/BK commit an empty group, touching no operand slot; its issue and done events still exist. Two prime groups and one group per local iteration preserve the two-group lookahead, including the short I/BK=1 case.

wait.meaning: Previous(t,i,q) collectively waits for its explicit MMA predecessor and rendezvous the CTA before refilling a previously consumed slot. q identifies the occurrence for noninitial local stages; the first stage has none.

acquire.meaning: Wait for the current payload-copy group, leaving at most two newer groups outstanding. Rendezvous the CTA and establish shared-to-async visibility for its payloads and synchronously staged scales. Done makes all four operand images readable. No tensor-box transaction wait is used.

mma.meaning: The elected warp-0 issuer copies both scale images into ScaleTM with four scale copies per operand, then issues four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of C2 and one cumulative completion commit. The first update initializes C2 without reading its old value. Done covers scale copies, operand reads and accumulator updates; same-issuer ordering makes each scale image available before its consuming update.

drain.meaning: Before c=0, wait for the final MMA commit and rendezvous the CTA. Each warp owns its TMEM quadrant, one row per lane. Load the next 32 columns into Fragment and wait for all those TMEM reads to retire, including padding rows.

emit.meaning: Convert Fragment to BF16 and directly store valid rows to RouteResult. Done consumes Fragment and submits the stores; kernel completion supplies global visibility. Padding rows produce no stores. There is no shared output sink.

close.meaning: Rendezvous all four warps after their last drain and direct store submission, before the next worktile resolves or primes. All data-bearing operand copies have been consumed; trailing empty groups may remain until later copy-group waits. Restart payload and scale slot indices at zero for the next worktile, while carrying MMA completion parity across worktiles.

retire.meaning: After the assigned sequence, warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this is a no-op. Prior drain and close actions have finished all TMEM reads; ordinary global stores finish with the kernel, without a bulk-store drain.

A worker with no assigned item still participates.

verb.load: Stage PayloadA from GatherQ and PayloadB as the two contiguous up/gate weight boxes. Arm the full-stage transaction count for 32768 payload bytes. Done covers both payload transfers. Payloads use three slots independently of the two scale slots.
verb.stage: Copy prepared weight scales into BScale's fused 128-row up/gate image, preserving the prepared ABI permutation. The lane-permuted 4-byte asynchronous copies collectively stage 2048 bytes. Done is their completion arrival to the full-stage protocol. Also issue an L2-only weight-scale hint two stages ahead when that stage lies in the same worktile; the hint has no consumer or completion edge.

retire.meaning: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this action is a no-op. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

guard.meaning:
Wait for PDL predecessor completion before loading the device Clean
verdict. Done supplies this worker's current verdict and selects the
bounded run domain; the guard executes even with no assigned payload.
It neither reads routed scratch nor allocates TensorStorage.

wait.meaning: Hoist=1 when R>=16*E, otherwise Hoist=0. Drain(t,q) completes after its explicit predecessors; q identifies the optional wait before the first scale copy of a worktile.

verb.prepare: The elected issuer waits for the full-stage protocol and copies AScale and BScale into ScaleTM: four scale-copy operations for each operand. Issuance includes submission of all scale copies; only then does this issuer advance to the MMA action. Done is covered by the following cumulative MMA completion.
verb.mma: Consume PayloadA/PayloadB and ScaleTM in four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates to C1. The first update initializes C1 without reading its old value. The fused 128-column product covers both up and gate. Issue a cumulative completion commit after each stage; done covers scale copies, payload reads and accumulator updates. The last stage also commits result readiness for the epilogue. Same-issuer ordering ensures an earlier MMA has consumed ScaleTM before a later scale copy overwrites that scale slot, and makes each scale copy visible before the MMA that uses it.

verb.drain: Each warp owns its hardware TMEM quadrant (warp index modulo four), one row per lane. For c=0 or 1, load the matching 32 up and 32 gate values into this quadrant's rows of Fragment, issue both reads before waiting, and wait for all their TMEM reads to retire. Done makes this register fragment usable.
verb.emit: Evaluate fc1_quantize for this 32-channel Fragment, including padding rows. For c=0 initialize ScalePack and retain its first two scale bytes; c=1 adds the last two, stores the full four-byte scale word on valid rows and resets it. Store valid payload bytes for each c. Done means local computation and store submission consumed Fragment; global stores can still be in flight. Invalid rows submit no output stores.
verb.release: This warp arrives once after its last TMEM-read wait and warp rendezvous. Done releases only this warp's accumulator quadrant; MMA reuse waits for all four epilogue roles. This warp immediately continues its final conversion/store tail without waiting for the other epilogue warps or for global output-store completion.

enter.meaning: Execute the PDL entry protocol before testing the assigned work. Since I/BK=1, each t is both one worktile and one continuous staging iteration. An empty assigned sequence allocates nothing, including when J>0 but this worker has no item. Otherwise initialize completion state, allocate TensorStorage from warp 0 and rendezvous all four warps.

prime.meaning: Resolve the first min(3,count(t)) assigned items into Metadata. Each lane retains five lookup fields: compact row origin, valid row extent, output column origin, and weight payload/scale coordinates. Advance the static assignment cursor once per resolved item; no shared row-index table is used. Empty work makes this action a no-op.

fetch.meaning: Using this item's Metadata, load both operands' scale images into the single ScalePrefetch register set. Load ActS for all BM rows, redirecting padding rows to the first valid row; load prepared gemm2_weights_scale for all BN2 columns. The previous prefetched set has already been published before this overwrite. These ordinary loads may overlap an issued MMA.

publish.meaning: Scatter ScalePrefetch into AScale and BScale for the indicated item and establish shared-to-async visibility. The register set is then reusable. Acquire supplies the CTA rendezvous before the current scale images are consumed.

verb.load: Warp 0 issues the ActQ and gemm2_weights tensor boxes from this item's Metadata into PayloadA and PayloadB. Arm completion for their combined 32768 bytes. Done covers both payload transfers; consecutive payload rows and padding follow the fc2 definition.

wait.meaning: Previous(t,q) or Final(b) waits for its explicit MMA predecessor and rendezvous all four warps before accumulator readout. Previous also protects the payload slot reused by item t+2 and the scale slot reused by item t+1. q identifies the noninitial-iteration wait. Final establishes TMEM read visibility.

commit.meaning: MetadataUpdate(t) commits the preceding iteration's Pending for item t+2 to Metadata(t+2), after the preceding item's readout and close. The new item aliases that preceding item's metadata slot; delaying the commit preserves its output coordinates. With no pending item this action touches no slot and is a no-op.

acquire.meaning: Wait for the current payload transaction completion, rendezvous the CTA and establish shared-to-async visibility for its scales. Done makes PayloadA, PayloadB, AScale and BScale readable.

mma.meaning: The elected warp-0 issuer copies both scale images into ScaleTM, then issues the four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of C2 and one cumulative completion commit. The first update initializes C2 without reading the previous item's accumulator. Done covers scale copies, operand reads and accumulator updates. Same-issuer ordering makes each scale image visible before its consuming update. Future scale fetch and metadata resolve may proceed while this MMA is in flight.

resolve.meaning: Resolve item t+3 into Pending if it belongs to this worker's assigned sequence, advancing the same cursor used by prime. Retain it until the next iteration's commit; do not overwrite Metadata here because the current item's epilogue still needs it. If no such item exists, touch neither Pending nor Metadata.

drain.meaning: Each warp owns its hardware TMEM quadrant, one row per lane. Load the next 32 columns into Fragment and wait for all these TMEM reads to retire, including padding rows.

emit.meaning: Convert Fragment to BF16 and directly submit valid-row stores to RouteResult using this item's Metadata. Done consumes Fragment; kernel completion supplies global visibility. Padding rows submit no stores, and there is no shared output sink.

close.meaning: Rendezvous all four warps after this item's last TMEM read and store submission. Its accumulator and metadata slots may now be reused, while ordinary global stores may remain in flight. Payload prefetch for later items is not drained here.

retire.meaning: After the final readout and close, warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. Every issued payload and scale load has been consumed. Empty assigned sequences make this action a no-op; global stores complete with the kernel, without a bulk-store drain.

verb.enter: All participating threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission. This grants no data readiness. The entry executes even if this worker has no payload work.
verb.produce: Each thread owns FinalWidth independent output elements. Hoist its eight route indices and scores, initialize Accumulator, then consume valid BF16 route vectors in increasing slot order using finalize's FMA recurrence. Convert and store Y once; no CTA reduction or inter-thread barrier is required. Empty routing still writes zeros.

verb.enter: Wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility, then warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. This does not publish this grid's output or verdict.
verb.check: Initialize each thread's Dirty accumulator to zero. Each thread first submits 16-byte zero stores for its flattened output words, without reading old output, then traverses payload words, scale bytes, scores and expert parameters in separate grid-stride loops, OR-ing verification's predicates. Test the clamp only when supplied. There is no CTA barrier between these loops. A final CTA-wide OR and rendezvous forms PreDirty after all threads have submitted output stores and completed their checks. Done does not imply global completion of the output stores.
verb.publish: Thread 0 contributes a dirty atomic OR only when PreDirty is nonzero, orders that contribution before an atomic arrival increment, and obtains an arrival ticket. The final ticket holder reads the accumulated dirty bit, stores PreState word 0 and resets the dirty and arrival words. It then performs the system-visibility fence and stores HostVerdict. Other ticket holders do not publish the verdict; every worker still completes this action. There is no global spin or CTA rendezvous here. Done covers this worker's protocol operations; only kernel_done guarantees all stripes' zero-output writes and verdict visibility.

verb.enter: After preverify.kernel_done and its global-storage handoff, wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility, then warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. This does not publish this grid's output or verdict.
verb.check: Initialize each thread's Dirty accumulator to zero. Each thread first submits 16-byte zero stores for its flattened output words, without reading old output, then traverses payload words, scale bytes, scores and expert parameters in separate grid-stride loops, OR-ing verification's predicates. Test the clamp only when supplied. There is no CTA barrier between these loops. A final CTA-wide OR and rendezvous forms BlockDirty after all threads have submitted output stores and completed their checks. Done does not imply global completion of the output stores.
verb.publish: Reuse PreState's reset words in place. Thread 0 contributes a dirty atomic OR only when BlockDirty is nonzero, orders that contribution before an atomic arrival increment, and obtains an arrival ticket. The final ticket holder reads the accumulated dirty bit, stores Clean and resets the dirty and arrival words. It then performs the system-visibility fence and stores HostVerdict. Other ticket holders do not publish the verdict; every worker still completes this action. There is no global spin or CTA rendezvous here. Done covers this worker's protocol operations; only kernel_done guarantees all stripes' zero-output writes and verdict visibility.

verb.enter: All participating threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission. Each thread executes the guard's additional predecessor wait and reads Clean. A clean verdict makes subsequent assigned work a no-op or empty, without payload or metadata accesses. This entry and both kernel milestones remain even for empty work.
verb.produce: For Clean=1 this action is a no-op with issue/done events and no Hist or Counts access. Otherwise zero Hist, synchronize the CTA, histogram valid routes, synchronize, then atomically add nonzero Hist entries into Counts.

verb.enter: All participating threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission. verb.produce: For Clean=1 this action is a no-op with issue/done events and no scratch or metadata accesses. Otherwise PrefixScratch holds 257 tile-prefix entries, two 64-word scan arrays and the tile total. Warp-local scans, the scan of warp totals and CTA rendezvous produce both prefixes. After their publication within the CTA, threads enumerate tile IDs by binary search and write Offs, TilePrefix, TileExpert and TileRow. J=0 still writes prefixes.

verb.enter: All participating threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission. Each thread executes the guard's additional predecessor wait and reads Clean. A clean verdict makes subsequent assigned work a no-op or empty, without payload or metadata accesses. This entry and both kernel milestones remain even for empty work.
verb.produce: For Clean=1 this action is a no-op with issue/done events and no map or scratch accesses. Otherwise Reservation contains batch counts, reserved bases and local ranks. Zero counts/ranks, CTA rendezvous, histogram, rendezvous, reserve intervals from Fill, rendezvous, then assign atomic local ranks and write all four maps defined by routing. No thread exits before the last rendezvous; invalid real routes still write RoutePos=-1.

verb.enter: All participating threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission. Each thread executes the guard's additional predecessor wait and reads Clean. A clean verdict makes subsequent assigned work a no-op or empty, without payload or metadata accesses. This entry and both kernel milestones remain even for empty work.
verb.produce: Each of the 128 threads handles one SourceChunk, reads its token's eight RoutePos entries, and loads a 16-byte source only if some route is valid. Replicate to those destinations; the same registers hold this chunk through all route stores. No inter-thread exchange.

verb.enter: First execute the guard's predecessor-grid wait and read Clean. For Clean=1, read no routing metadata and allocate no TensorStorage; all work domains are empty. The explicit PDL trigger is skipped, and grid completion supplies launch_ready. For Clean=0, repeat the predecessor wait and let warp 0 trigger dependent launches, then read J. If J=0, allocate no TensorStorage. Otherwise warp 0 initializes the shared completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage; all seven warps rendezvous before their independent work loops, including workers with no assigned item.
verb.prime: Resolve this worktile's expert and row base. The activation-scale source is GatherS. Load the first stage and, when the local stage count exceeds one, the second into APrefetch. All BM rows are loaded, redirecting padding scales to the first valid row. Prefetch registers are restarted per worktile.
verb.publish: Scatter the current APrefetch set into AScale, then establish shared-to-async visibility. If a next stage exists in this worktile, load it into the other register set before the warp rendezvous and full-stage arrival. Thus stage 1 is loaded again after being primed; the first primed copy is overwritten without use. Done includes this arrival, not completion of the independent payload/weight-scale loads.
verb.retire: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For Clean=1 or global J=0 this action is a no-op with issue/done events and no resource access. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

enter.meaning: First execute the guard's predecessor-grid wait and read Clean. For Clean=1, read no metadata and allocate no TensorStorage; work domains are empty and grid completion supplies launch_ready without an explicit trigger. For Clean=0, repeat the predecessor wait and let warp 0 trigger dependent launches, then read J. J=0 leaves the work domains empty without allocating TensorStorage. Otherwise initialize the shared completion protocol, allocate TensorStorage from warp 0 and rendezvous the CTA, including workers with no assigned item.

resolve.meaning: Resolve the expert and compact row base. Populate RowIndex for all BM rows, redirecting padding scale rows to base(j), then rendezvous the CTA. RowIndex remains live through this worktile's scale copies; payload boxes keep consecutive rows.

verb.stage: CopyGroup(t,s) commits one asynchronous scale-copy group. For s < I/BK, it stages AScale from ActS and prepared BScale from gemm2_weights_scale by four 4-byte copies per row and operand. Warp 0 also issues the ActQ and weight-payload tensor boxes, whose combined completion accounts for 32768 bytes. Payload and scale slots use the continuous stage g[t,s] modulo three; no scale-prefetch register buffer is used. Done covers these scale copies and payload transfers, before acquire's CTA publication. For s >= I/BK, only the empty copy group is committed; the action still has issue and done events and touches no slot. The first two groups prime each worktile. Each iteration then commits one more group, preserving the two-group lookahead even in the final two iterations.

wait.meaning: Previous(g,q) collectively waits for its explicit MMA predecessor and rendezvous the CTA before any slot refill. q identifies the occurrence for noninitial local stages; the first stage has none.

acquire.meaning: Wait for the current stage's scale-copy group, leaving at most two newer groups outstanding, and for both tensor boxes. Rendezvous the CTA and establish shared-to-async visibility. Done makes PayloadA, PayloadB, AScale and BScale readable.

mma.meaning: The elected warp-0 issuer copies both scale images into ScaleTM, then issues four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of C2 and one cumulative completion commit. The first update of each worktile initializes C2 without reading its previous value. Done covers scale copies, operand reads and accumulator updates. Same-issuer scale-copy/MMA ordering makes each scale image available before its consuming update.

drain.meaning: Before c=0, wait for the final MMA commit and rendezvous the CTA. Each warp owns its TMEM quadrant, one row per lane. Load this quadrant's next 32 columns into Fragment and wait for all those TMEM reads to retire, including reads for padding rows.

emit.meaning: Convert Fragment to BF16 and directly store the valid rows to RouteResult. Done consumes Fragment and submits the stores; global visibility is supplied by kernel completion. Padding rows produce no stores. There is no shared output sink.

close.meaning: Rendezvous all four warps after their last drain and direct store submission. Only then may the next worktile resolve and prime its operands. All payload and scale data copies for this worktile have been consumed; trailing empty copy groups have no data. Carry ring position and completion parity across worktiles.

retire.meaning: After the assigned sequence, warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For Clean=1 or global J=0 this action is a no-op with issue/done events and no resource access. Prior drain and close actions have finished all TMEM reads; ordinary global stores finish as part of kernel completion, without a bulk-store drain.

verb.enter: All participating threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission. verb.produce: For Clean=1 this action is a no-op with issue/done events: it neither reads routing data nor writes Y. Otherwise each thread owns FinalWidth independent output elements. Hoist its eight route indices and scores, initialize Accumulator, then consume valid BF16 route vectors in increasing slot order using finalize's FMA recurrence. Convert and store Y once; no CTA reduction or inter-thread barrier is required. Empty routing still writes zeros.

verb.enter: Execute the unconditional dependency-control wait and warp-0 trigger, both inert on this ordinary-stream path. Initialize each thread's DirtyBits to zero; do not reset global tickets here.
verb.produce: Cooperatively issue the shard's 16-byte YFirst stores using a flat grid stride. Done means store submission, not grid-wide output visibility; stores may remain in flight during the scans.
verb.compute: Accumulate zero_verify's payload, scale, score and parameter predicates in DirtyBits through four independent grid-stride sweeps. Every thread continues its scans after seeing dirt. A CTA-wide OR rendezvous converts the per-thread bits to FirstPartDirty. This also ensures every thread has issued its assigned zero stores.
verb.publish: One thread per CTA handles the persistent int32[4] device state: word 0 holds FirstClean, word 1 the dirty aggregate, word 2 the arrival count; word 3 is unused and unchanged. If FirstPartDirty is nonzero, atomically OR 1 into word 1. Publish this contribution before atomically incrementing word 2 once. The final ticket observes all preceding contributions, writes FirstClean into word 0 and resets words 1 and 2 to zero. It then establishes system visibility and stores FirstMirror in the pinned mirror. Nonfinal ticket owners return without waiting for other CTAs. Done is this CTA's protocol completion, not an early grid-ready event. probe.kernel_done covers every output store and verdict; the mirror store alone does not certify full output completion. Words 1 and 2 begin at zero from ABI creation or the prior final ticket. probe.kernel_done precedes verify's output and protocol writes, so no first-pass store or atomic remains in flight when the full graph replaces the first versions. The host observation only selects submission; it does not replace this completion edge.

verb.resolve: Resolve successive assigned worktiles using a stepped row-tile/column cursor equivalent to work_schedule's strided sequence. A descriptor contains the selected expert, compact row base, valid row bound and output-column origin; ordinary per-lane address encodings do not change these coordinates. Initial descriptors go to Metadata's three-slot ring. Later descriptors go to the single Pending register set, without overwriting the still-live ring entry. Metadata remains needed through that worktile's payload issue, scale fetch and output store submission.
verb.commit: Move the previously resolved Pending descriptor into Metadata. This occurs after the prior worktile's epilogue has finished reading the aliased ring entry, before new lookahead loads use this descriptor.
verb.fetch: Load ActS and the prepared weight-scale image for this worktile into the single APrefetch and BPrefetch register sets. All BM activation rows are read, redirecting padded rows to base(j); each operand contributes 2048 bytes. Registers are overwritten only after their previous values were scattered by publish. This synchronous fetch can overlap the previously issued MMA and payload transfers.
verb.publish: ScaleSM(t) scatters APrefetch and BPrefetch into AScale(t) and BScale(t) with their required scale permutations, then establishes shared-to-async visibility. The register sets are now reusable.

load.meaning: PayloadPair(t) issues two tensor transfers into PayloadA(t) and PayloadB(t), using Metadata(t) to select ActQ and the prepared FC2 weight box. Arm a transaction for 32768 bytes. Done covers both transfers. Two initial worktiles prime the ring; subsequent loads look two worktiles ahead, while the previous MMA has already retired.

verb.wait: Previous(t,q) waits for the preceding worktile's cumulative MMA completion and rendezvous all four warps; q marks its noninitial occurrence. Ready(t) waits for this worktile's payload transaction, rendezvous the CTA and establishes visibility for its shared scales. Final(t) waits for the last product, applies the tensor synchronization fence and rendezvous the CTA. None of these waits drains future lookahead transfers.

mma.meaning: Warp 0's elected issuer copies AScale(t) and BScale(t) to ScaleTM(t), four scale-copy operations per operand, then issues four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates to C2. The first update initializes C2 without reading its old value. Same-issuer ordering makes the scale copies visible to the consuming MMA. A cumulative completion commit covers scale copies, payload reads and accumulator updates.

verb.emit: Each warp drains its hardware TMEM quadrant into Fragment in BN2/32 successive 32-column chunks. Wait for every TMEM read, convert valid rows to BF16 and submit direct global vector stores to RouteResult; padding rows are read but not stored. Reuse each register fragment after its stores have consumed it. A final CTA rendezvous completes all TMEM reads and store submissions before C2 or the old descriptor is reused. Global output stores may remain in flight.
verb.retire: Deallocate TensorStorage only after the last epilogue and all assigned work. Empty workers have no allocation to retire, so this action is a no-op for them. All issued lookahead transfers belong to existing worktiles and have been consumed; no speculative tail is left to drain. Kernel completion supplies global RouteResult visibility.

enter.meaning: All participating threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission before the guard. This permission does not establish data readiness.

verb.produce: For Clean=1 this action is a no-op with no metadata, operand or output access. For Clean=0: Each thread owns FinalWidth independent output elements. Convert and store Y once; no CTA reduction or inter-thread barrier is required. Empty routing still writes zeros.

verb.scan:
Each thread initializes its DirtyAccumulator word to zero, submits
its strided 16-byte FirstZeroY stores, and accumulates dirty bits over
its assigned payload words, scale bytes, scores and parameters.
All threads participate in the CTA OR vote after the independent
scans, producing FirstCheck for this worktile. Done covers the vote and
zero-store submission; it does not claim global output completion.
verb.publish:
Thread 0 atomically ORs the shared global dirty word when FirstCheck is
nonzero, establishes device visibility, and atomically increments
the arrival word. The last ticket holder reads the accumulated dirty
word, writes FirstClean, then resets both reduction words for the next
verification. Establish system visibility before storing
FirstHostVerdict; this is not an output-completion signal.
Other ticket holders do not publish the final verdict. This protocol does not spin or require all CTAs to be
resident together. Kernel completion covers every zero store and
state update. The following graph starts after this kernel_done,
so the second verification reuses fully reset FirstState and may
overwrite FirstZeroY and FirstHostVerdict. A host timeout creates
no completion event and permits no concurrent device reuse.
This phase's DirtyAccumulator is worker-local; the next kernel
establishes independent worker and register-resource instances.

verb.scan:
Each thread initializes its DirtyAccumulator word to zero, submits
its strided 16-byte ZeroY stores, and accumulates dirty bits over
its assigned payload words, scale bytes, scores and parameters.

scans, producing Check for this worktile. Done covers the vote and
zero-store submission; it does not claim global output completion.
verb.publish:
Thread 0 atomically ORs the shared global dirty word when Check is
nonzero, establishes device visibility, and atomically increments
the arrival word. The last ticket holder reads the accumulated dirty
word, writes Clean, then resets both reduction words for the next
verification. Establish system visibility before overwriting
the pinned word with HostVerdict; no host poll follows it.
Other ticket holders do not publish the final verdict. This protocol does not spin or require all CTAs to be
resident together. Kernel completion covers every zero store and
state update; downstream guards wait for that full completion.
ZeroState remains available to downstream guards; same-stream
kernel order protects its next device use. HostVerdict has no
downstream device consumer here; a later graph_replay may reset
the pinned word from the host without waiting for this request
to complete. Publication consumes
FirstState's reset reduction words under the graph-boundary
dependency, without reading FirstClean or FirstZeroY.

verb.produce: Stage every route ID once into StagedIds and zero the full GroupTable, including the unused expert columns. After CTA rendezvous, warp g forms Hist(g) for its contiguous route group. verb.setup: Resolve the expert, row base and valid row count. Fill ScaleRow with base(j)+r for valid rows and base(j) for padding, then rendezvous the CTA. Keep it until this worktile's last scale copy.

stage.meaning: Operands(t,s) is one copy group. For s<count(i), stage ActQ into PayloadA and the prepared FC2 weight payload into PayloadB by two tensor transfers, with 32768 total expected bytes. All four warps asynchronously copy ActS and prepared weight scales directly into AScale and BScale, using ScaleRow for the activation scales. Each scale image has 2048 bytes. These four buffers hold version g[t,s] in its three-slot ring. Commit one scale-copy group; done covers both payload transfers and all scale copies. For s>=count(i), commit an empty group without operand access; its issue/done still exist. The first two groups prime the worktile; later groups refill two stages ahead, after the preceding MMA's completion.

verb.wait: Ready(g) waits for the matching scale-copy group and payload transaction, then rendezvous all four warps and establish shared-to-async visibility. The two later committed groups, including empty terminal groups, make the scale wait select this stage. Product(t) waits for the final cumulative MMA completion and rendezvous the CTA before any accumulator drain.

The first update of each worktile initializes C2 without reading it. A cumulative completion commit covers scale copies, payload consumption and accumulator updates. Same-issuer ordering makes each scale copy visible to its consuming MMA.

verb.emit: Each warp drains its hardware TMEM quadrant, one row per lane, in BN2/32 successive 32-column chunks. Wait for each TMEM read, convert valid rows to BF16 and submit direct global vector stores to RouteResult. Padding rows are read but not stored. enter.meaning: Execute the PDL entry protocol. For global J=0, allocate nothing and leave all work domains empty. Otherwise initialize the shared completion protocol, allocate TensorStorage from warp 0 and rendezvous the CTA, including workers with no assigned item.

resolve.meaning: Resolve the expert and compact row base. Populate RowIndex for all BM rows, redirecting padding rows to base(j), then rendezvous the CTA. Both ActQ payload and ActS scale loads use this map throughout the worktile.

scale.meaning: ScalePair(t,k) loads one 16-byte ActS row and four prepared 4-byte weight-scale words per operand row, then stores their complete AScale and BScale images in slot k modulo three. Preserve the prepared scale permutation and establish shared-to-async visibility. Done includes these synchronous loads, shared stores and the proxy fence; acquire supplies CTA-wide publication. No scale-prefetch buffer survives this action. The first two valid stages are primed; later scales are refilled after the MMA two stages earlier is issued, allowing the scale-load latency to overlap that MMA.

verb.stage: CopyGroup(t,s) submits 16-byte asynchronous copies for the complete PayloadA and PayloadB images of stage s into slot s modulo three, and commits one group. Use RowIndex for ActQ and the prepared weight-row mapping for gemm2_weights. Done covers the payload copies, before acquire's CTA publication. For s >= I/BK commit an empty group, touching no operand slot; its issue and done events still exist. Two prime groups and one group per local iteration preserve the two-group lookahead, including the short I/BK=1 case.

wait.meaning: Previous(t,i,q) collectively waits for its explicit MMA predecessor and rendezvous the CTA before refilling a previously consumed slot. q identifies the occurrence for noninitial local stages; the first stage has none.

acquire.meaning: Wait for the current payload-copy group, leaving at most two newer groups outstanding. Rendezvous the CTA and establish shared-to-async visibility for its payloads and synchronously staged scales. Done makes all four operand images readable. No tensor-box transaction wait is used.

mma.meaning: The elected warp-0 issuer copies both scale images into ScaleTM with four scale copies per operand, then issues four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of C2 and one cumulative completion commit. The first update initializes C2 without reading its old value. Done covers scale copies, operand reads and accumulator updates; same-issuer ordering makes each scale image available before its consuming update.

drain.meaning: Before c=0, wait for the final MMA commit and rendezvous the CTA. Each warp owns its TMEM quadrant, one row per lane. Load the next 32 columns into Fragment and wait for all those TMEM reads to retire, including padding rows.

emit.meaning: Convert Fragment to BF16 and directly store valid rows to RouteResult. Done consumes Fragment and submits the stores; kernel completion supplies global visibility. Padding rows produce no stores. There is no shared output sink.

close.meaning: Rendezvous all four warps after their last drain and direct store submission, before the next worktile resolves or primes. All data-bearing operand copies have been consumed; trailing empty groups may remain until later copy-group waits. Restart payload and scale slot indices at zero for the next worktile, while carrying MMA completion parity across worktiles.

retire.meaning: After the assigned sequence, warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this is a no-op. Prior drain and close actions have finished all TMEM reads; ordinary global stores finish with the kernel, without a bulk-store drain.

verb.enter: All participating threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission. This grants no data readiness. The entry executes even if this worker has no payload work.
verb.produce: Each thread owns FinalWidth independent output elements. Hoist its eight route indices and scores, initialize Accumulator, then consume valid BF16 route vectors in increasing slot order using finalize's FMA recurrence. Convert and store Y once; no CTA reduction or inter-thread barrier is required. Empty routing still writes zeros.

enter.meaning: Execute the PDL entry protocol before testing the assigned work. Since I/BK=1, each t is both one worktile and one continuous staging iteration. An empty assigned sequence allocates nothing, including when J>0 but this worker has no item. Otherwise initialize completion state, allocate TensorStorage from warp 0 and rendezvous all four warps.

prime.meaning: Resolve the first min(3,count(t)) assigned items into Metadata. Each lane retains five lookup fields: compact row origin, valid row extent, output column origin, and weight payload/scale coordinates. Advance the static assignment cursor once per resolved item; no shared row-index table is used. Empty work makes this action a no-op.

fetch.meaning: Using this item's Metadata, load both operands' scale images into the single ScalePrefetch register set. Load ActS for all BM rows, redirecting padding rows to the first valid row; load prepared gemm2_weights_scale for all BN2 columns. The previous prefetched set has already been published before this overwrite. These ordinary loads may overlap an issued MMA.

publish.meaning: Scatter ScalePrefetch into AScale and BScale for the indicated item and establish shared-to-async visibility. The register set is then reusable. Acquire supplies the CTA rendezvous before the current scale images are consumed.

verb.load: Warp 0 issues the ActQ and gemm2_weights tensor boxes from this item's Metadata into PayloadA and PayloadB. Arm completion for their combined 32768 bytes. Done covers both payload transfers; consecutive payload rows and padding follow the fc2 definition.

wait.meaning: Previous(t,q) or Final(b) waits for its explicit MMA predecessor and rendezvous all four warps before accumulator readout. Previous also protects the payload slot reused by item t+2 and the scale slot reused by item t+1. q identifies the noninitial-iteration wait. Final establishes TMEM read visibility.

commit.meaning: MetadataUpdate(t) commits the preceding iteration's Pending for item t+2 to Metadata(t+2), after the preceding item's readout and close. The new item aliases that preceding item's metadata slot; delaying the commit preserves its output coordinates. With no pending item this action touches no slot and is a no-op.

acquire.meaning: Wait for the current payload transaction completion, rendezvous the CTA and establish shared-to-async visibility for its scales. Done makes PayloadA, PayloadB, AScale and BScale readable.

mma.meaning: The elected warp-0 issuer copies both scale images into ScaleTM, then issues the four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of C2 and one cumulative completion commit. The first update initializes C2 without reading the previous item's accumulator. Done covers scale copies, operand reads and accumulator updates. Same-issuer ordering makes each scale image visible before its consuming update. Future scale fetch and metadata resolve may proceed while this MMA is in flight.

resolve.meaning: Resolve item t+3 into Pending if it belongs to this worker's assigned sequence, advancing the same cursor used by prime. close.meaning: Rendezvous all four warps after this item's last TMEM read and store submission. Its accumulator and metadata slots may now be reused, while ordinary global stores may remain in flight. Payload prefetch for later items is not drained here.

retire.meaning: After the final readout and close, warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. Every issued payload and scale load has been consumed. Empty assigned sequences make this action a no-op; global stores complete with the kernel, without a bulk-store drain.

verb.enter: Execute the PDL entry protocol before reading J. For J=0 there is no local allocation and all work domains are empty. Otherwise initialize completion state and allocate TensorStorage through warp 0, then rendezvous all four warps, including workers with empty assigned sequences. MMA completion parity starts once per worker and continues across its worktiles.
verb.setup: Resolve the expert, row base and valid row count. Fill RowMap with base(j)+r for valid rows and base(j) for padding, then rendezvous the CTA. Both activation payload and scale accesses use RowMap; keep it through this worktile's last operand access. Operand ring positions restart at zero for each worktile.

stage.meaning: Operands(t,s) is one payload-copy group. For s<count(i), all four warps copy ActQ into PayloadA and prepared FC2 weights into PayloadB in 16-byte chunks, 16384 bytes per operand. For the first two stages, issuance first synchronously loads and scatters ActS and prepared weight scales into AScale and BScale, 2048 bytes per operand, and establishes shared-to-async visibility. Later scale stages are filled by the loop tail. All four buffers use slot s%3. Commit one group for every action, including s>=count(i), when there are no operand accesses. Done covers the group's payload copies and any leading scale stores; empty groups retain issue/done events.

verb.wait: Ready(t,i) waits for the matching payload-copy group and rendezvous all four warps. Two later committed groups, including terminal empty groups, make this wait select stage i. Leading scales were published by their stage action; later scales were synchronously published in an earlier loop tail. Product(t) waits for the final cumulative MMA completion and rendezvous the CTA before any accumulator drain. Completion parity advances after every MMA wait, including Product.

mma.meaning: Warp 0's elected issuer establishes shared-to-async visibility, copies AScale and BScale into ScaleTM with four scale-copy operations per operand, then issues four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates to C2. The first update initializes C2 without reading its old value. A cumulative completion commit covers scale copies, payload consumption and accumulator updates. Same-issuer ordering makes each scale copy visible to its MMA.

verb.fill: ScalePair(t,s) is the pair AScale and BScale for the future stage s. After issuing the current MMA, all four warps synchronously load ActS and prepared weight scales through registers, scatter into slot s%3 and establish shared-to-async visibility. These loads can overlap the current MMA. Each activation row loads 16 bytes; each weight row loads four 4-byte words from its prepared scale image. Done covers all shared stores and publication. For s>=count(i), no scale accesses occur; this action is a no-op with issue/done.
verb.emit: Each warp drains its hardware TMEM quadrant, one row per lane, in BN2/32 successive 32-column chunks. Wait for each TMEM read, convert valid rows to BF16 and submit direct global vector stores to RouteResult. Padding rows are read but not stored. Reuse that warp's Fragment only after its current store instructions have consumed it. A final CTA rendezvous follows all chunks; done guarantees all TMEM reads and store submissions are finished, permitting the next worktile to reuse C2 and the operand rings. Global stores may remain in flight.
verb.retire: Warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage after the whole assigned sequence; for J>0 even an idle worker allocates and deallocates. For J=0 this is a no-op. Real operand copies have been consumed; terminal empty groups retain no resource accesses. Kernel completion supplies global RouteResult visibility.

Otherwise warp 0 initializes the shared completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage; all seven warps rendezvous once before entering their independent work loops. A worker with no assigned item still participates.
verb.prime: Resolve this worktile's expert and row base. Load the first GatherS stage and, when the local stage count exceeds one, the second into APrefetch. All BM rows are loaded, redirecting padding scales to the first valid row. Prefetch registers are restarted per worktile.
verb.publish: Scatter the current APrefetch set into AScale, then establish shared-to-async visibility. If a next stage exists in this worktile, load it into the other register set before the warp rendezvous and full-stage arrival. Thus stage 1 is loaded again after being primed; the first primed copy is overwritten without use. Done includes this arrival, not completion of the independent payload/weight-scale loads.
verb.retire: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this action is a no-op. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

verb.enter: Execute the PDL entry protocol before reading J. A worker whose assigned sequence is empty returns without local allocation, even when J>0. Otherwise warp 0 allocates TensorStorage, initializes completion state and joins all four warps at a CTA rendezvous. Ring positions and completion parity start once per worker. Because I=BK here, each t is both one worktile and one reduction stage.
verb.resolve: Resolve successive assigned worktiles using a stepped row-tile/column cursor equivalent to work_schedule's strided sequence. A descriptor contains the selected expert, compact row base, valid row bound and output-column origin; ordinary per-lane address encodings do not change these coordinates. Initial descriptors go to Metadata's three-slot ring. Later descriptors go to the single Pending register set, without overwriting the still-live ring entry. Metadata remains needed through that worktile's payload issue, scale fetch and output store submission.
verb.commit: Move the previously resolved Pending descriptor into Metadata. This occurs after the prior worktile's epilogue has finished reading the aliased ring entry, before new lookahead loads use this descriptor.
verb.fetch: Load ActS and the prepared weight-scale image for this worktile into the single APrefetch and BPrefetch register sets. All BM activation rows are read, redirecting padded rows to base(j); each operand contributes 2048 bytes. Registers are overwritten only after their previous values were scattered by publish. This synchronous fetch can overlap the previously issued MMA and payload transfers.
verb.publish: ScaleSM(t) scatters APrefetch and BPrefetch into AScale(t) and BScale(t) with their required scale permutations, then establishes shared-to-async visibility. The register sets are now reusable.

load.meaning: PayloadPair(t) issues two tensor transfers into PayloadA(t) and PayloadB(t), using Metadata(t) to select ActQ and the prepared FC2 weight box. Arm a transaction for 32768 bytes. Done covers both transfers. Two initial worktiles prime the ring; subsequent loads look two worktiles ahead, while the previous MMA has already retired.

verb.wait: Previous(t,q) waits for the preceding worktile's cumulative MMA completion and rendezvous all four warps; q marks its noninitial occurrence. Ready(t) waits for this worktile's payload transaction, rendezvous the CTA and establishes visibility for its shared scales. Final(t) waits for the last product, applies the tensor synchronization fence and rendezvous the CTA. None of these waits drains future lookahead transfers.

mma.meaning: Warp 0's elected issuer copies AScale(t) and BScale(t) to ScaleTM(t), four scale-copy operations per operand, then issues four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates to C2. The first update initializes C2 without reading its old value. Same-issuer ordering makes the scale copies visible to the consuming MMA. A cumulative completion commit covers scale copies, payload reads and accumulator updates.

verb.emit: Each warp drains its hardware TMEM quadrant into Fragment in BN2/32 successive 32-column chunks. Wait for every TMEM read, convert valid rows to BF16 and submit direct global vector stores to RouteResult; padding rows are read but not stored. Reuse each register fragment after its stores have consumed it. A final CTA rendezvous completes all TMEM reads and store submissions before C2 or the old descriptor is reused. Global output stores may remain in flight.
verb.retire: Deallocate TensorStorage only after the last epilogue and all assigned work. Empty workers have no allocation to retire, so this action is a no-op for them. All issued lookahead transfers belong to existing worktiles and have been consumed; no speculative tail is left to drain. Kernel completion supplies global RouteResult visibility.

verb.enter: Execute the PDL entry protocol before reading J. For J=0 there is no local allocation and all work domains are empty. Otherwise initialize completion state and allocate TensorStorage through warp 0, then rendezvous all four warps, including workers with empty assigned sequences. Ring position and completion parity start once per worker and continue across its worktiles.
verb.setup: Resolve the expert, row base and valid row count. Fill ScaleRow with base(j)+r for valid rows and base(j) for padding, then rendezvous the CTA. Keep it until this worktile's last scale copy.

stage.meaning: Operands(t,s) is one copy group. For s<count(i), stage ActQ into PayloadA and the prepared FC2 weight payload into PayloadB by two tensor transfers, with 32768 total expected bytes. All four warps asynchronously copy ActS and prepared weight scales directly into AScale and BScale, using ScaleRow for the activation scales. Each scale image has 2048 bytes. These four buffers hold version g[t,s] in its three-slot ring. Commit one scale-copy group; done covers both payload transfers and all scale copies. For s>=count(i), commit an empty group without operand access; its issue/done still exist. The first two groups prime the worktile; later groups refill two stages ahead, after the preceding MMA's completion.

verb.wait: Ready(g) waits for the matching scale-copy group and payload transaction, then rendezvous all four warps and establish shared-to-async visibility. The two later committed groups, including empty terminal groups, make the scale wait select this stage. Product(t) waits for the final cumulative MMA completion and rendezvous the CTA before any accumulator drain.

mma.meaning: Warp 0's elected issuer copies AScale and BScale to ScaleTM, four scale-copy operations per operand, then issues four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates to C2. The first update of each worktile initializes C2 without reading it. A cumulative completion commit covers scale copies, payload consumption and accumulator updates. Same-issuer ordering makes each scale copy visible to its consuming MMA.

verb.emit: Each warp drains its hardware TMEM quadrant, one row per lane, in BN2/32 successive 32-column chunks. Wait for each TMEM read, convert valid rows to BF16 and submit direct global vector stores to RouteResult. Padding rows are read but not stored. Reuse that warp's Fragment only after its current store instructions have consumed it. A final CTA rendezvous follows all chunks; done guarantees all TMEM reads and store submissions are finished, permitting the next worktile to reuse C2 and the operand rings. Global stores may remain in flight.
verb.retire: Warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage after the whole assigned sequence; for J>0 even an idle worker allocates and deallocates. For J=0 this is a no-op. Kernel completion supplies global RouteResult visibility; no bulk-store sink or separate bulk completion protocol is used.

verb.produce: FormatTables comprises E2Table, ScaleTable and ScalePairTable. Each thread evaluates one byte code and issues all three corresponding global table stores. There is no shared table staging or inter-thread data dependence. Done covers evaluation and store submission; tables.kernel_done supplies completed writes and visibility before the host publishes readiness or the direct consumer starts. No table entry is released or overwritten by this request after publication.

verb.inspect: Unit(v) resolves the statically assigned u(v), route, intermediate chunk and current expert ID. Define ValidUnit(v)=1 for an in-range expert and 0 otherwise. Invalid units have no following payload or synchronization actions. The cached token identity starts invalid and changes only on a valid unit's input preparation.
verb.prepare: If this valid unit changes the cached token, decode its entire X from global packed input and scales through the completed global E2Table and ScaleTable, and have one thread count its valid routes into TokenCount. Retain X and TokenCount while the token is unchanged. InputCache includes H/8 unused padding elements. Complete a CTA rendezvous on every valid unit, including a cache hit. Any previous token's input reads finished before this slot can change.
verb.contract: Execute fc1 using all sixteen warps, with two up/gate pairs per warp and the 32 reduction groups mapped across its lanes. Weight payloads and scales are read directly from global memory through E2Table and ScaleTable; no shared weight buffer is allocated. Group starts at zero for this unit. After its local reduction, publish UpGate to shared memory and rendezvous all warps before activation.
verb.quantize: Warp zero consumes UpGate, evaluates activate and forms the two independent 16-channel maxima. It publishes the B FP32 QChunk values, then all sixteen warps rendezvous. UpGate is now consumed; QChunk remains live until every FC2 hidden stripe has read it.
verb.accumulate: Each thread computes four consecutive hidden channels at a time, traversing the next stripe after 2048 channels. Read each unit's packed FC2 weight slice and scales directly from global memory, decoding through E2Table and ScaleTable, consume QChunk, and issue scalar FP32 atomic additions of Partial into RouteAccum. All H channels are covered. Done means this CTA's additions have been issued and QChunk's local reads have ended; publication to other CTAs is completed by arrive.
verb.arrive: Every thread publishes its own RouteAccum additions to device scope, then the CTA rendezvous orders those publications before one elected thread increments Arrivals[t]. Record Last=1 exactly for the ticket n(t)*S-1 and 0 otherwise; publish it to all threads with a CTA rendezvous. The last-arrival consumption ordering makes all n(t)*S units' contributions visible before final reads. This protocol does not wait for other CTAs to reach a grid barrier. Last(v,a) names this unit's returned flag for the nested occurrence a.
verb.gather: Only the last unit executes this action. One thread collects valid flattened route indices into prelude's Exchange.FinalRoutes and their current routing weights into FinalScores in increasing slot order. The census already consumed Exchange.WarpCounts. Rendezvous before any thread reads the finalizer metadata.
verb.finalize: Execute fc2_finalize in four-hidden-element stripes: initialize the current stripe of Z in OutputSum, read the completed route sums, cast each route value to BF16 before its weighted FP32 FMA, reset each consumed route accumulator stripe, and write the BF16 output stripe. Finish the CTA's output and reset store submissions, rendezvous, then one thread resets Arrivals[t]. No output scratch array is created. Global completion and visibility to later requests are supplied by the single kernel's completion.
verb.advance: Rendezvous all sixteen warps after every valid unit, including a non-last unit that did no finalization. This protects Last, TokenCount, UpGate, QChunk and finalizer metadata before subsequent units reuse them. The elected finalizer has submitted its counter reset before this rendezvous completes; no per-unit global wait or grid synchronization is inserted.

verb.produce: FormatTables comprises E2M1Pair, E4M3Float and E4M3Pair. Each thread evaluates one byte code and writes its three table entries directly to the module globals. Each BF16 pair occupies one packed 32-bit word with pair 0 in the low half. Temporary values stay in registers; there is no shared staging or inter-thread exchange. Done covers this role's stores; kernel_done supplies their global completion and visibility.

FormatTables denotes E2M1Pair, E4M3Value and E4M3Pair together. Each thread computes one byte code's entries and writes them to their separate global arrays. No table entry depends on another; there is no CTA exchange or shared scratch. The kernel's completion makes all entries visible to the device synchronization.

FormatTables denotes TableE2Pair, TableE4 and TableE4Pair. Each thread computes and stores one byte-code entry of all three tables. No input tensor, shared buffer, inter-thread exchange or table read is required. Kernel completion makes all entries visible to the subsequent host device wait.

FormatTables denotes FormatPair, FormatScale and FormatScalePair. Each thread evaluates one byte code by format_tables and writes its three entries to global storage, packing each BF16 pair into one 32-bit word. Values are computed in registers and need no inter-thread exchange or shared staging. Done consumes those temporaries and submits the stores; kernel_done supplies global completion and visibility before the host device wait returns.

FormatTables denotes E2Pair, E4Float and E4Pair. Each lane computes and writes one byte code's entries from format_tables; there is no tensor input, inter-thread exchange, staged buffer or dependency-control instruction. Kernel completion covers all stores before the host's device synchronization returns.

FormatTables denotes E2M1Pair, E4M3Float and E4M3Pair together. Each thread evaluates format_tables for one byte code and stores that entry of all three arrays directly to their global storage. Each BF16 pair is one 32-bit word, pair index 0 in its low half. There is no shared staging or inter-thread exchange. Kernel completion makes every table entry visible before the host resumes.

FormatTables denotes the joint output Table4, Table8 and Table8Pair. Each thread evaluates format_tables for one byte code, packs each BF16 pair into one 32-bit word and writes the three global entries. Entries are disjoint; no shared buffer or intra-CTA rendezvous is needed. Kernel completion makes all stores visible before the host synchronization returns; no table read or release occurs in this request.

FormatTables denotes FormatFP4, FormatScale and FormatScalePair together. Each participating thread computes one code's entries by format_tables and writes all three global tables. The BF16 pairs occupy two lanes of a 32-bit stored word. No input tensor is read, no local value survives its stores, and no inter-thread exchange or PDL trigger is used. Kernel completion makes every table entry visible.

Conversion temporaries are consumed immediately; there is no shared staging or inter-thread exchange. Done includes all conversion and store submissions; tables.kernel_done supplies global visibility before host publication of table readiness.

Each lane evaluates format_tables for its distinct byte pattern and writes that entry of F4Pair, F8Value and F8Pair. All 256 entries are covered without shared storage, inter-thread exchange or PDL entry/launch-permission operations. Scalar temporaries die after these stores; kernel completion supplies table visibility before the host service boundary and subsequent computation.

verb.enter: All threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. This does not grant data readiness.
verb.load: Four neighboring threads own each 16-channel quantization block, with four up and four gate channels per thread. For every in-range backing row, load both slice vectors into PartialLoad before the expert-ID test. Out-of-range packet lanes do no reads; unused route rows still load allocated backing bytes. Done means these vectors are available locally.
verb.produce: Read PackedExpert's backing row and reject out-of-range IDs before any per-expert parameter access. Accepted groups merge the retained slices into Merged in ascending order, then compute merge_quantize into Activated. Four-lane maximum exchange combines all 16 absolute values; paired neighbor exchange assembles packed payload words. Store ActQ and one ActS byte per accepted block, including unused backing rows that pass the check. No cross-block or cross-CTA exchange is needed. Rejected groups perform no arithmetic or stores, but the action still completes. PartialLoad is dead after the merge; Merged is dead after activation; Activated is dead after quantization and store submission.

verb.enter: All threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility, then warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. When global J=0, skip local allocation and all work loops. Otherwise initialize completion state, allocate TensorStorage and rendezvous all four warps, including workers whose assigned sequence is empty. Payload/scale ring position and MMA completion parity start once here and continue across worktiles.
verb.compute: Rows(t) resolves the worktile expert and base(j), then fills RowIndex[r] with base(j)+r for r<valid(j) and base(j) otherwise. All four warps rendezvous before using it for scale loads. RowIndex survives through this worktile's scale staging; payload boxes use consecutive rows directly and do not use RowIndex.

stage.meaning: Future(t,q) always commits one asynchronous-copy group. For q<I/BK, issue four 4-byte copies per row for each scale operand into AScale and BScale. RowIndex selects ActS rows; prepared weight-scale addressing preserves the Contract permutation. One elected thread issues the consecutive ActQ box and prepared-weight box into PayloadA and PayloadB, with a joint payload transaction count of (BM+BN2)*(BK/2) bytes. All four objects use slot g[t,q]%3. Done covers both payload transactions and the scale copies, which have distinct completion mechanisms. For q>=I/BK there are no data transfers or resource accesses, but the empty group commit and its events remain. The two leading groups precede the main loop; each iteration then issues the group two stages ahead, so the wait with two newer groups outstanding retires the current scale group even at the tail. There is no register scale-prefetch slab.

verb.wait: Prior(t,i,u) waits for the explicit previous-stage MMA completion and rendezvous of all four warps; u names its noninitial-stage occurrence. Stage(g) waits for that stage's scale-copy group and payload-byte completion, then rendezvous and establish visibility to the tensor operation. Result(t) waits for the last MMA commit and rendezvous before any accumulator reads. These waits preserve carried completion parity; none is an early dependent-grid launch permission.

contract.meaning: For C2(g), the elected warp-0 issuer copies AScale and BScale into ScaleTM, then issues the four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of fc2. The first update of each worktile initializes C2 without reading old accumulator data. Commit one cumulative completion covering scale copies, payload reads and accumulator writes. Same-issuer ordering makes the scale copies visible to their MMA consumers. No other warp is an independent producer or epilogue role.

verb.release: Worktile(t) rendezvous all four warps after all fragment reads and direct-store submissions. This permits the next worktile to overwrite C2, RowIndex and operand slots; no next-work prime is issued before this point. Global stores may remain in flight.
verb.retire: After the whole assigned sequence, warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For J=0 this is a no-op; for J>0 an empty worker still retires its allocation. All MMA and TMEM reads have retired, and every issued data-copy group has been consumed. Kernel completion covers the direct global stores; empty copy-group commits need no payload drain.
verb.produce: For RouteResult(t), each warp independently walks BN2/32 consecutive 32-column chunks. Read its hardware quadrant, one row per lane, into Fragment and wait for those TMEM reads to retire. Read all BM rows, including padding; convert to BF16 with round-to-nearest-even and directly store only rows r<valid(j). The next chunk reuses that warp's Fragment after store submission has consumed it. Warps need no rendezvous between chunks. Done covers all chunk reads, conversions and store submissions, with global visibility supplied by kernel completion. No shared output sink or bulk output store is used.

Partition byte codes among the eight warps. For each code compute and store FormatPair, FormatScale and FormatScalePair as defined by format_tables, with no input tensor reads or previous-table reads. The stores cover all entries in device module storage. There is no shared buffer or cross-role dependency; init.kernel_done provides completion and visibility for the host synchronization.

If a next stage exists in this worktile, load it into the other register set before the warp rendezvous and full-stage arrival. Thus stage 1 is loaded again after being primed; the first primed copy is overwritten without use. Done includes this arrival, not completion of the independent payload/weight-scale loads.
