verb.produce:
FormatTables denotes the joint output E2M1Pair, E4M3Float and
E4M3Pair. The CTA evaluates all byte codes and directly stores
their entries in the module-global arrays defined by tables.
No input staging or inter-thread exchange is needed. Kernel
completion and the following device synchronization
provide visibility; no table operand is passed to the later phases.

verb.scan:
Initialize each thread's EligibilityLane predicate accumulator,
evaluate eligibility's tests over the scheduled independent input
loops, and perform a CTA-wide predicate OR. Every thread joins,
including threads without input elements. The result is EligibilityPart.
verb.publish:
If EligibilityPart is nonzero, the elected thread stores 1 into
the zero-initialized global EligibilityDirty. A clean shard does
not write that word; this action still has issue/done events.
Done covers only this shard's contribution. There is no arrival
counter or grid spin; eligibility.kernel_done supplies completion
and visibility for the subsequent synchronized host readback.

verb.produce: FormatTables denotes E2M1Pair, E4M3Float and E4M3Pair together. Each thread evaluates format_tables for one byte code and stores its three entries in the device-global arrays. The BF16 components of each pair occupy the low and high halves of one 32-bit entry. No table entry depends on another thread; there is no shared staging, inter-thread exchange or local retention beyond these stores. Done covers conversion and store submission; init.kernel_done covers all table writes and their visibility. The host device synchronization waits for this completion before continuing the rebuilding prefix.

verb.compute: Initialize each thread's DirtyBits to zero, then accumulate eligibility_scan's predicates over the assigned token rows, scores, parameters and both weight-scale sweeps. All threads finish every assigned sweep even after detecting dirt. The final CTA-wide OR rendezvous forms ProbePartDirty.
verb.publish: If ProbePartDirty is nonzero, one thread writes 1 to the temporary device ProbeDirty word; clean shards perform no store, preserving its service-established zero. The action and its events still occur in every submitted CTA. This is a plain conditional store, with no atomic aggregation or arrival-ticket protocol. Each CTA returns without waiting for other CTAs; eligibility.kernel_done covers all scan reads and any flag writes before the host readback and deallocation.

verb.enter: Execute the unconditional dependency-control wait and warp-0 trigger, both inert on this ordinary-stream path. Initialize each thread's DirtyBits to zero; do not reset global tickets here.
verb.produce: Cooperatively issue the shard's 16-byte YFirst stores using a flat grid stride. Done means store submission, not grid-wide output visibility; stores may remain in flight during the scans.
verb.compute: Accumulate zero_verify's payload, scale, score and parameter predicates in DirtyBits through four independent grid-stride sweeps. Every thread continues its scans after seeing dirt. A CTA-wide OR rendezvous converts the per-thread bits to FirstPartDirty. This also ensures every thread has issued its assigned zero stores.
verb.publish: One thread per CTA handles the persistent int32[4] device state: word 0 holds FirstClean, word 1 the dirty aggregate, word 2 the arrival count; word 3 is unused and unchanged. If FirstPartDirty is nonzero, atomically OR 1 into word 1. Publish this contribution before atomically incrementing word 2 once. The final ticket observes all preceding contributions, writes FirstClean into word 0 and resets words 1 and 2 to zero. It then establishes system visibility and stores FirstMirror in the pinned mirror. Nonfinal ticket owners return without waiting for other CTAs. Done is this CTA's protocol completion, not an early grid-ready event. probe.kernel_done covers every output store and verdict; the mirror store alone does not certify full output completion. Words 1 and 2 begin at zero from this ABI creation. probe.kernel_done precedes verify's output and protocol writes, so no first-pass store or atomic remains in flight when the full graph replaces the first versions. The host observation only selects submission; it does not replace this completion edge.

verb.produce: FormatTables comprises TablePair, TableScale and TableScalePair. Each participant evaluates one byte code and stores the three corresponding entries in the persistent global arrays. The two BF16 halves use one packed word per pair. No participant reads another's result; there is no shared buffer, barrier or PDL trigger. Done covers local evaluation and store submission; tables.kernel_done provides global completion and visibility for the host's device synchronization. Temporary values die with the worker; table storage is not released at kernel exit.

Initialize per-participant DirtyBits, scan the assigned row payloads and scales, then the separate route-weight, expert parameter and two weight-scale word traversals of eligibility. Read the clamp only when present. Fold with a CTA-wide OR; one elected participant writes 1 to ScanDirty for a dirty group, and a clean group submits no store. Other groups do not wait or read ScanDirty. Done covers this group's reads and conditional store submission; scan.kernel_done supplies global visibility for the subsequent host readback. The private registers die with this worker; the separate global scalar survives until the host copy has returned.

Each thread computes one byte code's entries in TableE2Pair, TableE4 and TableE4Pair and writes them directly to module global memory. Done covers computation and submission of all three stores; kernel_done and the host device wait establish publication of the complete tables.

Traverse this shard's input subsets and accumulate lane-local dirty predicates, without reading route IDs or weight payloads. All 256 threads participate in a CTA boolean-OR rendezvous. One thread publishes 1 to ProbeDirty when ProbePart is nonzero; a clean shard performs no global store. The action and its completion event remain present for clean and empty subsets. ProbeDirty is consumed by the host helper, not by a GEMM role.

FormatTables denotes FormatPair, ScaleFloat and ScalePair. Each thread owns one byte code, evaluates format_tables and directly stores that code's two BF16 pairs and FP32 scalar to the three device-global arrays. Each BF16 pair is packed into one 32-bit word, with pair element 0 in its low half. Threads require no exchange, shared buffer or PDL protocol. Kernel completion makes all stores visible to the host's following device synchronization.

verb.inspect: Initialize one DirtyLane word per participating thread to zero. Visit the assigned token payload words with magnitude-bit masking and their scale bytes; then inspect scores, expert parameters and optional limits, followed by stored FC1 and FC2 scale words. OR each predicate into its lane state without early exit. No conversion table is read.
verb.produce: Collectively OR all DirtyLane predicates at a CTA rendezvous to form ProbePart; one lane stores 1 to global ProbeDirty only when that part is dirty. A clean stripe still executes this action and its completion event but writes no verdict. Kernel completion supplies visibility for a reached host readback. No PDL entry or launch-ready signal belongs to this scan.

FormatTables denotes E2M1Pair, E4M3Float and E4M3Pair from
format_tables. Each of the 256 threads computes the entries
for its byte value, rounds the three BF16 values and stores
the low/high pair, FP32 scale and duplicated BF16 scale pair
in their global arrays. No thread reads another thread's
entries; no CTA barrier, shared tile or local reuse protocol
is needed. Done includes computation and store submission;
kernel completion establishes the tables' global visibility.

Initialize one unsigned rejection state per thread. Threads stride
through the shard's token-row payload words and scale bytes, then its
routing weights, expert parameters and both prepared scale arrays.
Payload words retain only the eight E2M1 magnitude fields; packed
scale words test all four bytes. Optional clamp loads occur only when
HasLimit=1. Accumulate every predicate locally without an early exit.
All 256 threads participate in the CTA-wide OR, including threads
with no assigned elements. One thread sets ProbeDirty to 1 if this
OR rejects; otherwise no global store occurs. No CTA polls the word
or waits for another CTA. Completion includes this local scan and
conditional store; kernel completion supplies host-visible readiness.
The fixed source uses non-atomic shared-flag stores, so this design
records the monotone publication without asserting race-free execution.

FormatTables denotes FormatPair, FormatScale and FormatScalePair. Each thread owns one code entry and evaluates the tables rewrite, writing that entry of all three global tables. The scalar conversions are local to the thread, with no shared staging or inter-thread exchange. Done submits all three stores; kernel_done supplies their global visibility before the device synchronization returns. No table storage is released at this worker's exit.

Initialize each thread's ProbeFlags word to zero. Each thread accumulates its assigned predicates through the five scan passes, retaining its word between passes. Payload loads examine four bytes together and ignore each nibble's sign bit; weight-scale loads examine four encoded scales together. Threads whose local ranges are empty retain zero. A CTA-wide Boolean OR and rendezvous form ProbePart; only the designated leader publishes 1 to global ProbeDirty when the partial is nonzero. There is no cross-CTA rendezvous or PDL entry. Done consumes the local flags and submits any verdict store; kernel completion supplies visibility for host inspection. A zero partial still completes this action but does not write the flag.

FormatTables denotes the joint production of E2M1Pair, E4M3Value and E4M3Pair from format_tables. Each thread owns one byte code, computes its three entries and stores them directly to the global tables. No inter-thread exchange, shared staging, or local retained buffer is needed. Done covers those stores; kernel_done supplies their completion and visibility at the host service boundary.

Initialize every thread's Predicate to zero and accumulate zero_probe tests through all assigned local passes. Threads cover each token's payload in four-byte words and its scales bytewise, then their scalar and four-scale packet positions. Skip the clamp read when absent. No early exit or reset between local passes occurs. The final CTA-wide OR rendezvous computes DirtyPart; thread 0 writes 1 to global Dirty only when it is nonzero. Done covers this store and all input reads; kernel_done establishes the visibility required for a successful host readback.

FormatTables denotes E2M1Pair, E4M3Float and E4M3Pair together. Each thread computes and writes the three entries for one code. All 256 codes are covered exactly once, with no shared staging or cross-thread reduction. Done covers computation and store submission; kernel_done guarantees global completion for the following device-synchronization service.

Initialize each thread's ScanBits to zero. Cooperatively scan assigned token payload words and scale bytes, then independent score and expert sequences, then FC1 and FC2 scale-word sequences. Keep predicate bits across these loops without early exit; the optional clamp is read only when present. A CTA-wide OR produces ProbePartial. One thread writes one to ProbeDirty if the OR is nonzero; a clean shard leaves the initialized flag unchanged. Done covers the reduction and store submission; kernel_done supplies the global completion used by the following chain.

FormatTables denotes PairTable, ScaleTable and ScalePairTable. Each thread computes its byte-code entry and submits the three module-global stores, packing the two BF16 components into one word for each pair table. No inter-thread exchange, CTA barrier or local persistent buffer is needed. Done covers conversions and store submission; kernel_done supplies complete table visibility for the following device-wide synchronization.

Initialize each thread's ThreadBad to zero. Cooperatively scan this stripe's payload and input-scale rows, then route weights, expert parameters, FC1 weight scales and FC2 weight scales. Payload is read in 4-byte words with both nibble sign bits masked out; weight scales are tested four bytes per word. Accumulate predicates in registers without early exit or rereading the global flag. All threads join one CTA-wide OR vote after their assigned reads, including threads with empty sequences. If ProbePart is nonzero, the leader submits the idempotent store of 1 to ProbeDirty; otherwise no store occurs. Done covers all local reads, the vote and any store submission. Kernel completion supplies flag visibility for host readback. There is no PDL entry, inter-CTA barrier or local buffer reuse.

FormatTables denotes FormatPair, FormatScale and FormatScalePair together.
Each of the 256 participating threads computes one byte-code entry and
submits its three global stores. Entries are independent and have no
inter-thread exchange or shared staging. Done covers computation and
store submission; kernel_done supplies visibility before the host's
device synchronization returns. No request tensor is read or modified.

Initialize one unsigned predicate accumulator per participating thread
in ScanAccum. Cooperatively read and test this shard's assigned inputs,
carrying each accumulator across all local loops without early exit.
A CTA-wide any reduction and rendezvous produce ProbePart. The elected
writer contributes 1 to global Dirty only for a nonzero part; a zero
part submits no store. No member reads Dirty, and no CTA waits for
another shard. Done covers the shard's reads, reduction and any store
submission; kernel completion supplies visibility for host readback.
Even a shard without tests completes the reduction with zero.

FormatTables denotes the three outputs FormatPair, FormatScale and FormatScalePair of format_tables. Each participant generates one code's entries and submits their global stores. There is no input load, shared buffer, inter-participant exchange or local reuse boundary. Done covers local conversion and store submission; kernel_done supplies completion and visibility for the device-wide synchronization in work_schedule. The table storage remains owned by the device module after this worker exits.

Initialize one ScanFlags word per participant. Accumulate the zero_probe tests over this worktile's separate local loops without early exit. Payload loads cover four bytes at a time; activation scales cover one byte, while prepared weight scales cover four bytes per load. Scores and present parameters are tested as FP32. The flag words remain live across every loop. A CTA-wide OR rendezvous forms ProbePart; one participant marks global ProbeDirty as 1 when it is nonzero. A clean CTA submits no flag store, but this action and its completion still exist. No CTA consumes another CTA's partial flag. The source uses concurrent plain stores for the common mark; the logical idempotent OR does not certify that lowering.

FormatTables denotes FormatPair, FormatScale and FormatScalePair together. The eight warps partition the 256 byte codes, evaluate format_tables and write every entry to its device-global module array. No invocation tensor, shared staging buffer or cross-thread exchange is needed. Done covers computation and store submission; kernel_done makes the table writes visible before the host device synchronization returns. The arrays remain allocated after this role exits.

Initialize every participating thread's LocalDirty to zero. Visit the zero_scan traversals in their stated order, OR-ing payload magnitude bits and nonfinite tests into that register; there is no early exit after finding dirt. Perform one CTA-wide Boolean OR, yielding ScanBad for this shard. A single thread stores 1 to the preinitialized global ScanDirty only when the collective predicate is true; all such stores have the same value. Done includes the collective and any store submission; kernel completion supplies host-read visibility. Other shards need no intermediate result, and LocalDirty is dead after the collective. This action remains present for clean shards although it makes no global store.

FormatTables denotes the three format_tables outputs FormatPair,
FormatScale and FormatScalePair. Independently evaluate each byte
code and store its entries directly to the module-global arrays.
No call-input read, inter-warp exchange, shared buffer, PDL trigger
or asynchronous operand operation is involved. Done covers all
local evaluations and store submissions; init_tables.kernel_done
supplies their global completion before the host synchronization
in work_schedule returns.

verb.scan:
Initialize the per-thread ProbeLane accumulators, walk the shard's
row-wise payload and activation scales, then the independent score,
parameter and prepared weight-scale streams defined by zero_probe.
Read the clamp stream only for HasLimit=1. All threads participate in
the final CTA-wide predicate OR, including threads with no elements,
to form ProbePart; no per-shard result array is materialized.
verb.publish:
An elected thread stores 1 to the separately initialized global
ProbeDirty only when ProbePart is nonzero. A zero part makes this action
a no-op with issue/done events; every part is zero in this accepted
selection. No shard reads ProbeDirty or waits for another shard.
Done covers this shard's contribution; probe.kernel_done and the host
synchronization in work_schedule cover the whole scan before readback.
This ordinary launch has no PDL trigger or persistent local resource.

verb.enter: All threads wait for predecessor-grid completion and visibility; warp 0 grants dependent launch permission before streaming starts.
verb.store:
Walk this shard's output units and submit the ZeroOutput stores.
Done means the local store loop has finished issuing its writes; global
output visibility is guaranteed by verify.kernel_done.
verb.scan:
Initialize one DirtyLane bit accumulator per thread. Independently
walk payload, activation-scale, score and expert-parameter packets in that
order, accumulating zero_verify's tests. Read clamp parameters only for
HasLimit=1. A CTA-wide predicate OR, including all threads even those
with no elements, produces DirtyPart.
verb.publish:
The elected thread atomically contributes a dirty bit if DirtyPart
is nonzero, orders that contribution before taking one global arrival
ticket, and then takes the ticket. The last arriving CTA observes the
combined dirty state, writes Clean, and resets both counters for reuse.
It also performs the optional pinned-mirror publication defined by verify.
Other CTAs complete after their own contributions, without waiting for
the last arrival. Done covers this CTA's state updates, not other CTAs'
output stores; only verify.kernel_done exposes Clean and ZeroOutput to
later grids. Counter reuse requires the previous execution and all its
flag readers to have completed through the existing stream ordering.

verb.produce: FormatTables denotes TableE2M1, TableE4 and TableE4Pair together. Evaluate format_tables for disjoint byte codes and write each code's three results directly to their module-global tables. Each BF16 pair occupies one 32-bit word, in component order. No input loads, shared staging or inter-warp exchange are needed. Done covers local computation and store submission; kernel_done supplies full table-write completion for the host synchronization.

verb.check: Initialize each thread's Dirty accumulator to zero. For each owned token row, scan payload words and then activation-scale bytes. Separately scan scores, parameters, FC1 weight-scale words and FC2 weight-scale words, retaining the accumulated predicates throughout. Each weight word tests all four scale bytes. There is no early exit after a dirty test. A CTA-wide OR and rendezvous yields ProbeBlockDirty after all threads finish their reads; even empty stripes participate.
verb.publish: If ProbeBlockDirty is nonzero, thread 0 submits an ordinary store of 1 to the shared global ProbeDirty word. All contributing stores carry the same value; clean stripes leave its initialized zero unchanged. A clean stripe still executes this action with issue/done events and no store. No atomic or inter-CTA rendezvous is performed. Done covers this worker's store submission; kernel_done covers the completed scan and visibility for the subsequent host observation.

verb.enter: Wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility, then warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. This does not publish this grid's output or verdict.
verb.check: Initialize each thread's Dirty accumulator to zero. Each thread first submits 16-byte zero stores for its flattened output words, without reading old output, then traverses payload words, scale bytes, scores and expert parameters in separate grid-stride loops, OR-ing verification's predicates. Test the clamp only when supplied. There is no CTA barrier between these loops. A final CTA-wide OR and rendezvous forms BlockDirty after all threads have submitted output stores and completed their checks. Done does not imply global completion of the output stores.
verb.publish: Thread 0 contributes a dirty atomic OR only when BlockDirty is nonzero, orders that contribution before an atomic arrival increment, and obtains an arrival ticket. The final ticket holder reads the accumulated dirty bit, stores Clean and resets the dirty and arrival words. If Mirror=1 it then performs the system-visibility fence and stores HostVerdict. Other ticket holders do not publish the verdict; every worker still completes this action. There is no global spin or CTA rendezvous here. Done covers this worker's protocol operations; only kernel_done guarantees all stripes' zero-output writes and verdict visibility.

verb.produce: TableEntries comprises PairTable, ScaleTable and ScalePairTable. Each thread evaluates init_tables for one distinct byte code and writes its three device-global entries. Intermediate conversions are local temporaries; there is no shared buffer, barrier or lookup-table read. Done covers this role's store submissions; init.kernel_done and the following device synchronization establish completion of every table write.

verb.compute: Initialize one uint32 ProbeBits value per thread to zero. Traverse this shard's token payload and activation-scale loops, then the flat score, expert-parameter and two weight-scale loops defined by zero_probe. A weight word supplies four byte tests. Preserve each thread's bits across every loop without early exit. A CTA-wide OR rendezvous forms ProbePart after all assigned reads finish; every thread reaches it.
verb.produce: If ProbePart is nonzero, thread zero stores int32(1) into the previously zeroed global ProbeDirty; otherwise this action is a no-op with its completion event still present. All dirty writers store the same value. There is no read-modify-write, final-arrival counter, reset or inter-CTA wait in this kernel. Done means store submission by this shard, not grid visibility. probe.kernel_done and the caller-stream synchronization cover all contributions before readback and temporary-storage release.

Each participant owns one byte code and computes that entry in all three tables by format_tables. TableEntries names this set of three results. Store them directly to module-global arrays; there is no task-input read, CTA exchange or shared staging. Done covers local computation and store submission; kernel_done supplies completion and visibility before the host device wait returns. No later phase of this node reads these arrays.

verb.compute: Initialize DirtyBits, scan the worktile's payload and input-scale rows, then the separate score and expert-parameter loops, and finally both weight-scale word spaces. Each participant retains its predicate bits across these loops; a CTA-wide OR produces ProbeDirtyGroup. An absent clamp is never dereferenced. Done covers all reads and the block reduction. No output is written.
verb.publish: One elected participant writes 1 to global ProbeDirty only when this group's predicate is dirty. Otherwise this action is a no-op with a completion event. The source uses an ordinary same-value store; this is not an atomic arrival or grid barrier. Done covers this group's contribution, not the whole reduction. The grid completion and subsequent stream synchronization precede the host readback and release of the temporary scalar.

verb.enter: Wait for the preceding grid's completion and visibility, then warp 0 grants dependent launch permission without promising Clean or output readiness.
verb.produce: Verification combines this worktile's ZeroPacket stores and DirtyGroup calculation. Initialize each participant's DirtyBits, then each participant issues its zero stores and scans its strided payload words, scale bytes, route weights and expert parameters. A CTA-wide OR predicate reduction produces DirtyGroup after these traversals. The clamp is read only when present; route_ids and weight tensors are not read. Done covers the predicate reduction and store submission; output visibility is supplied by kernel_done.
verb.publish: One elected thread contributes a dirty bit to VerifyState when needed, establishes device visibility and atomically takes an arrival ticket. The last arriving CTA reads the aggregate, writes Clean and resets both aggregation words. If a host mirror is bound, it then uses system visibility before writing the same verdict there. Other CTAs do not write Clean or the mirror. Done covers this CTA's contribution; Clean and all ZeroPacket writes become externally usable at verify.kernel_done. The unused VerifyState word is unchanged.

verb.produce:
Tables denotes PairTable, ScaleTable and ScalePairTable.
Each thread computes one byte code's two nibble decodes and
scale decode, then writes that entry in each module-global
array. The two BF16 values of each pair share one 32-bit
word in low-then-high order. Only per-entry temporaries are
needed; no shared buffer, inter-thread exchange, operand ring
or atomic update participates. Done covers computation and
store submission. Kernel completion covers all table writes;
the host's full-device wait completes before the ready-set
publication and later service prefix.

verb.scan:
Initialize each thread's accumulator to zero. For each owned
activation row, stream its payload words then scale bytes;
next scan the flat scores, parameters and the two weight-scale
arrays independently. OR predicates locally, then perform a
CTA-wide OR vote to form ProbeCheck. There is no early scan
exit, output write, operand ring or table access.
verb.publish:
After the CTA vote, thread zero writes one to the global
ProbeDirty word only for a dirty part. A clean part performs
no store, but this action still completes. The fixed source
uses same-value plain stores for dirty contributors, without
a race-free guarantee for overlapping dirty writers.
No CTA waits for another CTA. Kernel completion, followed by
the host stream wait, bounds the readback and lifetime of the
provisional word; no device consumer treats it as Clean.

verb.scan:
Each thread initializes its DirtyAccumulator word to zero, submits
its strided 16-byte ZeroY stores, and accumulates dirty bits over
its assigned payload words, scale bytes, scores and parameters.
All threads participate in the CTA OR vote after the independent
scans, producing Check for this worktile. Done covers the vote and
zero-store submission; it does not claim global output completion.
verb.publish:
Thread 0 atomically ORs the shared global dirty word when Check is
nonzero, establishes device visibility, and atomically increments
the arrival word. The last ticket holder reads the accumulated dirty
word, writes Clean, then resets both reduction words for the next
verification. When MirrorWords=1 it establishes system visibility
before storing HostVerdict; this is not an output-completion signal.
Other ticket holders do not publish the final verdict. This protocol does not spin or require all CTAs to be
resident together. Kernel completion covers every zero store and
state update; downstream guards wait for that full completion.
ZeroState and the optional mirror survive through all consumers and
are reused only after the preceding same-stream request completes.

verb.enter:
First wait for predecessor-grid completion and read Clean. Clean=1
completes this entry without an explicit launch trigger, J read or
local allocation; launch_ready is then supplied by kernel completion.
Otherwise execute the PDL wait/trigger pair, then read global J.
For J=0 perform no local allocation and leave work domains empty.
For J>0 warp 0 initializes completion state and allocates TensorStorage;
all seven warps rendezvous before their independent work loops,
including workers with no assigned item. Ring positions persist
across the worker's worktiles.
verb.prime: Resolve this worktile's expert and row base. The activation-scale source is GatherS in fc1 and ActS in fc2. Load the first stage and, when the local stage count exceeds one, the second into APrefetch. All BM rows are loaded, redirecting padding scales to the first valid row. Prefetch registers are restarted per worktile.
verb.publish: Scatter the current APrefetch set into AScale, then establish shared-to-async visibility. If a next stage exists in this worktile, load it into the other register set before the warp rendezvous and full-stage arrival. Thus stage 1 is loaded again after being primed; the first primed copy is overwritten without use. Done includes this arrival, not completion of the independent payload/weight-scale loads.
verb.retire: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For Clean=1 or global J=0 this action is a no-op. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

enter.meaning: Execute the PDL entry protocol. If global J=0, perform no local allocation; subsequent work domains are empty. Otherwise warp 0 initializes the shared completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage; all seven warps rendezvous once before entering their independent work loops. A worker with no assigned item still participates.

verb.load: Stage PayloadA from ActQ and PayloadB from the selected FC2 weights. Arm the full-stage protocol for 32768 bytes; done covers both tensor transfers. Padding payload rows remain consecutive while AProducer redirects their scale rows. The coupled reuse wait gates payload issue and the following weight-scale staging at a two-stage distance, although payload storage has three slots. No weight-payload L2 hint is issued here.
verb.stage: Copy the prepared FC2 scale image with 16-byte asynchronous copies, four per lane, into BScale. Done includes the copy-completion arrival in the full-stage protocol; no independent scale-prefetch hint.

retire.meaning: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this action is a no-op. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

enter.meaning: Execute the PDL entry protocol. If global J=0, perform no local allocation; subsequent work domains are empty. Otherwise warp 0 initializes the shared completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage; all seven warps rendezvous once before entering their independent work loops. A worker with no assigned item still participates.

wait.meaning: Drain(t,q) completes after the four explicit prior-work accumulator releases. q identifies the one noninitial-work wait, before the first scale copy.

verb.prepare: The elected issuer waits for the full-stage protocol and copies AScale and BScale into ScaleTM: four scale-copy operations for each operand. Issuance includes submission of all scale copies; only then does this issuer advance to the MMA action. Done is covered by the following cumulative MMA completion.
verb.mma: Execute four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of C2, with first-update initialization and cumulative stage completion. Done covers preceding scale copies and operand reads; last-stage commit also publishes the result. Same-issuer scale-copy/MMA ordering protects ScaleTM reuse and copy-to-MMA visibility.

retire.meaning: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this action is a no-op. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

verb.enter: Execute the PDL entry protocol. If global J=0, perform no local allocation; subsequent work domains are empty. Otherwise warp 0 initializes the shared completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage; all seven warps rendezvous once before entering their independent work loops. A worker with no assigned item still participates.
verb.drain: Each warp owns its hardware TMEM quadrant (warp index modulo four), one row per lane. Read the single 32-column chunk c into that quadrant's rows of Fragment and wait for its TMEM reads to retire. Padding rows are read too; done makes Fragment usable.
verb.release: After all four chunks have been drained and their direct stores submitted, rendezvous this warp and arrive once to release its accumulator quadrant. Next-work scale preparation waits for all four epilogue roles; kernel completion supplies global store visibility.
verb.emit: For valid rows, convert Fragment to BF16 and submit direct stores into the matching 32-column RouteResult region. Padding rows perform no conversion or stores. Done means store submission has consumed Fragment; global stores may still be in flight.
verb.retire: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this action is a no-op. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

A worker with no assigned item still participates.

verb.release: After all four chunks have been drained and their direct stores submitted, rendezvous this warp and arrive once to release its accumulator quadrant. Next-work scale preparation waits for all four epilogue roles; kernel completion supplies global store visibility.
verb.emit: For valid rows, convert Fragment to BF16 and submit direct stores into the matching 32-column RouteResult region. Padding rows perform no conversion or stores. Done means store submission has consumed Fragment; global stores may still be in flight.
verb.retire: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this action is a no-op. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

verb.enter: Execute the PDL entry protocol. If global J=0, perform no local allocation; subsequent work domains are empty. Otherwise warp 0 initializes the shared completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage; all seven warps rendezvous once before entering their independent work loops. A worker with no assigned item still participates.
verb.drain: Each warp owns its hardware TMEM quadrant (warp index modulo four), one row per lane. Read the single 32-column chunk c into that quadrant's rows of Fragment and wait for its TMEM reads to retire. Padding rows are read too; done makes Fragment usable.
verb.release: After all four chunks have been drained and their direct stores submitted, rendezvous this warp and arrive once to release its accumulator quadrant. Next-work scale preparation waits for all four epilogue roles; kernel completion supplies global store visibility.
verb.emit: For valid rows, convert Fragment to BF16 and submit direct stores into the matching 32-column RouteResult region. Padding rows perform no conversion or stores. Done means store submission has consumed Fragment; global stores may still be in flight.
verb.retire: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For global J=0 this action is a no-op. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or a new global memory fence; kernel completion supplies the external visibility.

verb.produce: Initialize each thread's Dirty accumulator to zero. Cooperatively traverse the assigned activation rows, scores, parameters and both weight-scale word spaces, OR-ing zero_probe's predicates. A final CTA-wide OR and rendezvous forms ProbePartial. Thread 0 stores one to ProbeDirty only for a nonzero contribution; all other cases still complete this action without a global store. No output is touched. Done covers local reads and any store submission; kernel_done closes all scan accesses before the host readback and release of the temporary global scalar.

verb.scan:
Initialize each thread's DirtyAccumulator word to zero, visit its
assigned token rows and flat chunks, and combine the probe predicates.
Read weight-scale words and inspect all four bytes; no tensor scan is
skipped after a dirty observation. All eight warps participate in the
CTA dirty vote, producing this worktile's ProbeCheck. There are no
shared operand buffers, asynchronous transfers or output writes.
verb.publish:
After the CTA vote, thread 0 writes 1 to the shared ProbeDirty
only for a nonzero ProbeCheck; otherwise this action is a no-op
with its issue/done events intact. The selected accepted scan leaves
the initialized zero unchanged. There is no atomic arrival counter,
last-CTA reduction or inter-CTA spin. Done covers this worktile's
store submission. kernel_done and the following host stream
synchronization cover all verdict writes before readback and release
of the temporary allocation. Every subsequent verification has new
worker-local register resources and separate device-state storage.

verb.produce:
Initialize each thread's LocalBad to zero. Cooperatively evaluate all
assigned zero_probe tests: four payload bytes per word, bytewise activation
scales, scalar scores and expert parameters, then four scale bytes per
word for each weight tensor. Keep each thread's rejection state across
all these loops; do not exit after detecting a bad value. Skip limit
accesses when the input is None. A CTA-wide OR rendezvous forms ProbeBad;
one thread contributes 1 to global ProbeDirty for a bad bucket, and a
clean bucket performs no global store. Buckets with no data still execute
the rendezvous and this action's events. Done consumes LocalBad and
covers any store submission; scan.kernel_done supplies external visibility.
The global word's initialization, host consumption and cleanup are the
service boundary specified by work_schedule, not a CTA-local reset.

Initialize every lane's LocalFlags to zero, accumulate the zero_probe
checks over the assigned input families, and perform one CTA-wide Boolean OR.
Payload checks load four packed bytes together; weight-scale checks load four
scale bytes together. Lanes traverse their in-range indices with stride 256
within each token or their globally strided family. There is no early exit
after a failed check. Each nonzero group has its leader publish one to the
already initialized global ProbeDirty; zero groups issue no verdict store.
The action completes even for a group without failures. Kernel completion
covers all verdict stores; the helper's readback/cleanup is external to this role.
LocalFlags dies after the vote. The scalar's lifetime covers the scan's accesses
and any attempted host copy, without adding a cross-CTA barrier.

verb.compute:
Initialize each thread's Predicate to zero and OR tests from its
assigned input elements. Token payload words and activation scales
use row-local strides; the separate score, parameter and two
weight-scale loops use flat packet strides. Test all four bytes of
each weight-scale word. The optional clamp input is accessed only
when enabled. All eight warps rendezvous in a CTA-wide predicate OR,
producing ProbePart for this shard, including shards with no token row.
verb.produce:
One thread contributes one to the prezeroed global ProbeDirty word
when ProbePart is nonzero; a clean shard leaves it unchanged. There
is no arrival counter, last-shard winner, inter-CTA wait or PDL
trigger. Done finishes the shard's conditional store submission;
probe.kernel_done covers all contributions and visibility for the
subsequent synchronized host readback. The word is not reused for
Clean and is freed after that readback.

verb.enter: All threads wait for predecessor completion and visibility; warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. This trigger does not publish the verdict or output.
verb.produce: Stream the shard's ZeroOutput region with 16-byte zero stores, covering all caller output elements exactly once across shards. Stores may remain in flight until kernel completion.
verb.compute:
Keep one Predicate accumulator per thread across the separate payload,
activation-scale, route-weight and parameter scans. Start each at zero,
OR its dirty tests, then perform a CTA-wide OR rendezvous to obtain Dirty(b).
The optional clamp input is accessed only when enabled.
verb.fold:
One thread contributes Dirty(b) to the global dirty-OR word when nonzero,
orders that contribution before its atomic arrival ticket with a device
fence, and takes one ticket. The last arrival reads the combined dirty
word, writes Clean, and resets the dirty word and arrival counter to zero.
Other arrivals perform no verdict store. With a nonzero pinned mirror,
the winner executes a system fence then a volatile store of the same
verdict. Done means this shard's contribution and any winner tail are
finished; it does not imply that other shards' output stores have drained.
Only verify.kernel_done makes the complete ZeroOutput and Clean available
to downstream guards. State reuse follows same-stream execution ordering,
not the early trigger or the optional host-mirror store.

verb.inspect:
Initialize each lane's LocalProbe to zero and accumulate every
predicate in its assigned rows and packets using the probe definition.
Reuse the registers across the consecutive input passes without early
exit. Finish with a CTA-wide predicate reduction and rendezvous to form
ProbeFailure; there is no PDL trigger or dependency wait in this kernel.
verb.record:
An elected lane stores 1 to the globally initialized ProbeDirty
only for a nonzero ProbeFailure. Other lanes do not store. This accepted
node has zero contributions, so the service-initialized flag remains zero;
the record action still executes and completes in each CTA. Done retires
this CTA's contribution; probe.kernel_done plus the host synchronization
covers every shard before readback and frees no storage before its last use.

verb.inspect: Start after the caller-stream zero initialization of ProbeDirty. Each thread starts FailureBits at zero, scans its assigned payload/scale, score, parameter and weight-scale elements, and accumulates failed predicates. Within each token row, payload and scale loops precede advancing to the next row; the remaining flat loops follow. No CTA exits early on a failed predicate. Done makes each thread's failure contribution available for the CTA rendezvous.
verb.publish: A CTA-wide OR rendezvous combines FailureBits into ScanDirty. If it is nonzero, the elected thread writes 1 to the common ProbeDirty; otherwise this group leaves it untouched. On this accepting path every group still completes its scan and rendezvous, even when it has no token rows. This action's done covers the group's store submission, while probe.kernel_done and the host synchronization cover all device accesses before readback and free. No PDL launch permission or verifier-state write is produced by the probe.

verb.enter: Wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility, then let warp 0 signal dependent-grid launch permission. The completed probe and subsequent caller-stream initialization precede this entry; launch permission alone does not expose the new verdict.
verb.inspect: Write this worktile's zero-output region, then scan its independently strided input spaces and accumulate predicate failures in per-thread FailureBits. A CTA-wide OR rendezvous combines these bits into VerifyDirty after all threads have finished their scans and zero-store submissions. No weight or route-ID access is added.
verb.publish: The elected thread contributes a dirty bit with global atomic OR when needed, establishes global ordering, then atomically increments the arrival counter. The last arrival reads the combined dirty word, writes Clean, and resets dirty and arrival words to zero. If HostMirror=1 it establishes system visibility before writing CleanMirror; nonlast workers do not write either final verdict. The saved int32[4] zflag workspace holds Clean, dirty, arrival and one unused word. Publication initially zeroes it; later invocations reuse the last-arrival reset only after prior guards have finished. No worker spins waiting for other verifier CTAs. This action completes each worker's contribution; verify.kernel_done, not one worker's done or launch_ready, exposes the complete output and verdict.

verb.enter: All threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility, then warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. When global J=0, skip local allocation and all work loops. Otherwise initialize MMA completion state, allocate TensorStorage and rendezvous all four warps, including workers whose assigned sequence is empty. MMA completion parity starts once here and continues across worktiles; payload and scale slots restart at zero for each worktile after the preceding worktile release.
verb.compute: Rows(t) resolves the worktile expert and base(j), then fills RowIndex[r] with rr(j,r) from fc2. All four warps rendezvous before using it. Both ActQ payload and ActS scale loads use this same map, so every padded row repeats the first valid route. RowIndex survives through all payload and scale staging of this worktile.

stage.meaning: Payload(t,q) always commits one asynchronous-copy group. For q<I/BK, cooperatively copy the BM-row ActQ payload selected by RowIndex and the BN2-row prepared weight payload into PayloadA and PayloadB at slot q%3. Prepared weight addressing preserves the Contract permutation. Each operand row contributes BK/2 bytes in 16-byte transfers. Done covers these payload copies. For q>=I/BK, issue no transfers or resource accesses, but retain the empty commit and its events. Two leading groups precede the main loop; each iteration issues the group two stages ahead. There are no tensor-map payload transactions or scale copies in these groups.

verb.wait: Prior(t,i,u) waits for the explicit previous-stage MMA completion and rendezvous of all four warps; u names its noninitial-stage occurrence. Stage(t,i) waits until the current payload group has completed with two newer groups outstanding, then rendezvous all four warps and establish tensor-operation visibility for the payload and the synchronously staged scales. Result(t) waits for the last MMA commit and rendezvous before accumulator reads. These waits preserve carried MMA completion parity; they do not grant dependent-grid launch permission.

contract.meaning: For C2(t,i), the elected warp-0 issuer copies AScale and BScale into ScaleTM(t,i), then issues the four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of fc2. The first update of each worktile initializes C2 without reading old accumulator data. Commit one cumulative completion covering scale copies, payload reads and accumulator writes. Same-issuer ordering makes the scale copies visible to their MMA consumers. No other warp is an independent producer or epilogue role.

verb.release: Worktile(t) rendezvous all four warps after all fragment reads and direct-store submissions. This permits the next worktile to overwrite C2, RowIndex and operand slots starting at slot zero; no next-work prime is issued before this point. Global stores may remain in flight.
verb.retire: After the whole assigned sequence, warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For J=0 this is a no-op; for J>0 an empty worker still retires its allocation. All MMA and TMEM reads have retired and all issued data-copy groups have been consumed. Kernel completion covers direct global stores; empty copy-group commits need no payload drain.
verb.produce: For RouteResult(t), each warp independently walks BN2/32 consecutive 32-column chunks. Read its hardware quadrant, one row per lane, into Fragment and wait for those TMEM reads to retire. Read all BM rows, including padding; convert to BF16 with round-to-nearest-even and directly store only rows r<valid(j). The next chunk reuses that warp's Fragment after store submission has consumed it. Warps need no rendezvous between chunks. Done covers all chunk reads, conversions and store submissions, with global visibility supplied by kernel completion. No shared output sink or bulk output store is used.
verb.load: Scale(t,q), for q<I/BK, synchronously reads all BM rows of ActS and all BN2 rows of prepared weight scales into AScale and BScale at slot q%3, preserving the prepared-scale permutation. Each row contributes BK/Block scale bytes. Register intermediates are transient within this action, with no separate prefetch slab. Establish generic-shared-store visibility to the async proxy. Up to two leading scale stages are filled before the main loop; refill q=i+2 is after current-stage MMA issuance and can overlap it. The preceding-stage MMA retirement protects this slot from its previous reader. For q>=I/BK, perform no reads, writes or resource accesses; the action is a completed no-op.

verb.enter: All threads wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission. Read J and the assigned-work bounds. A worker with no assigned work returns before any local allocation or operand access, even when other workers have work.
verb.allocate: Initialize the payload and cumulative MMA completion protocol once, allocate TensorStorage, then rendezvous all four warps. Ring positions and completion parity span the whole assigned sequence. In this selection I=BK, so work ordinal t is also the continuous stage ordinal.
verb.prime: Resolve assigned work p into Metadata(p). Each logical record holds compact row base, remaining expert-row count, output-column origin, expert weight coordinate, and BN2 prepared-weight scale offsets. These encode the existing tile maps and prepared ABI; they do not allocate or claim another worktile.
verb.fetch: For ScalePrefetch(p), use Metadata(p) to read one stage of ActS into APrefetch and prepared gemm2_weights_scale into BPrefetch. Rows r>=valid(j) read ActS at base(j). Both register sets are usable on done and survive until publish:ScalePair(p); the next fetch reuses them only after that publication has consumed their values.
verb.publish: Scatter APrefetch and BPrefetch into AScale(p) and BScale(p), preserving the prepared scale permutation, then establish shared-to-async visibility. Done releases the register prefetch sets. The subsequent stage wait includes the CTA rendezvous needed before the elected issuer consumes these shared scales.

load.meaning: For PayloadPair(p), one elected thread issues the consecutive ActQ box and prepared gemm2_weights box into PayloadA(p) and PayloadB(p), using Metadata(p), with a joint transaction count of (BM+BN2)*(BK/2) bytes. Done covers both payload transfers. Padding follows math_reshape.fc2; no SMEM row-index array or asynchronous scale-copy groups are used. Loads can cross work boundaries without draining the payload ring.

verb.wait: Prior(t,q) waits for the explicit preceding MMA completion, carries its parity forward, and rendezvous all four warps; q names the noninitial-work occurrence. Stage(t) waits for that payload pair's transaction completion, then rendezvous all four warps and establish tensor-operation visibility of payloads and staged scales. Final waits for the last cumulative MMA completion and rendezvous before its accumulator reads. None of these waits grants data readiness merely from dependent-grid launch permission.
verb.produce: For RouteResult(p), use Metadata(p) to address compact output rows. Each warp walks BN2/32 chunks, reading its hardware TMEM quadrant, one row per lane, into Fragment and waiting for the TMEM reads to retire. All BM rows are read; only r<valid(j) is converted and directly stored as BF16. Store submission consumes the fragment before the next chunk overwrites it. After all chunks, rendezvous all four warps. Done releases C2 and this work's metadata, but global stores may remain in flight until kernel completion.
verb.advance: For Lookahead(t), copy the previously resolved PendingMetadata(t+2) into Metadata(t+2) when 1<=t and t+2<count(t). Its old occupant belongs to t-1, whose epilogue has now finished. Otherwise this action completes without reading or writing metadata.

contract.meaning: For C2(t), the elected warp-0 issuer copies AScale(t) and BScale(t) into ScaleTM(t), then issues the four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of math_reshape.fc2. The first update initializes C2 without reading old accumulator data. Commit one cumulative completion covering scale copies, payload reads and accumulator writes. Same-issuer ordering makes the scale copies visible to their MMA consumers.

verb.resolve: Resolve assigned work p into PendingMetadata(p), with the same fields as prime. Keep this result separate from Metadata(p) until advance, because the ring's old occupant is still needed by the previous work's epilogue. This register-only lookahead may overlap the current MMA.
verb.retire: After the final epilogue rendezvous, warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. Every issued payload pair has been consumed, every scale prefetch published, and all MMA and TMEM reads have retired. Direct global stores become externally visible at kernel completion.

verb.enter:
All participating threads wait for predecessor grid completion and
visibility; warp 0 then grants dependent-grid launch permission.
This grants no data readiness and executes even with no payload work.
verb.inspect:
Each thread first submits its assigned 8-element ZeroPacket stores,
then streams its payload-word, scale-byte, score and parameter indices.
Initialize its LocalDirty word to zero and accumulate the tested dirty bits;
retain it through the CTA-wide Boolean reduction. No route IDs, expert
weights or weight scales are read. Each input is checked at execution time.
verb.publish:
Reduce LocalDirty to this shard's DirtyPart with a CTA-wide OR.
Verification uses a persistent four-int32 global state holding Clean, a dirty
accumulator, an arrival counter and one unused word. It was zeroed before
ABI publication. A dirty CTA leader atomically ORs the dirty accumulator
with one. Every CTA leader then performs a device release fence and
atomically increments the arrival counter exactly once.
The last ticket holder reads the combined dirty word, publishes Clean,
and resets the dirty accumulator and arrival counter to zero for the next invocation. Non-last CTAs
do not spin or wait for other CTAs, so the grid need not be co-resident.
If Mirror=1, the last leader also performs a system fence and writes
HostVerdict in pinned host memory; otherwise that store has no elements.
This action does not assert that one CTA's arrival makes other CTAs'
zero stores globally complete. verify.kernel_done supplies full-grid
completion and visibility for all output stores and the device verdict.
The state and optional mirror remain allocated with the reused ABI;
same-stream execution completes this grid and all its guard readers before
the next verification can overwrite Clean. No host polling occurs here.

verb.enter: Wait for predecessor grid completion and visibility, then let warp 0 grant dependent-grid launch permission. This permission does not publish the verdict or zero output.
verb.store: Submit vector zero stores for this partition of ZeroOutput. Done means its stores have been submitted; verify.kernel_done provides global output visibility.
verb.compute: Initialize the per-thread DirtyBits to zero and OR predicates across each independent flat traversal in the scheduled order. CTA-wide OR and rendezvous produce PartialDirty; all threads participate even when their individual ranges are empty.
verb.fold: One thread per CTA atomically ORs a nonzero PartialDirty into ZState word 1, then establishes device visibility before incrementing arrival word 2. A zero partition still fences and increments the ticket. Only the final arrival reads the accumulated dirty bit, writes word 0 and resets words 1 and 2. If HasHost=1 it performs a system-scope fence before the volatile HostVerdict store. Earlier arrivals do not wait for the last; this action completes their own contribution, and verify.kernel_done closes the entire reduction and output writes. Word 3 is untouched.

verb.enter:
Execute the predecessor-completion/visibility helper, then warp 0
issues the dependent-launch trigger. With no pending predecessor
or with the recorded attribute disabled, the wait is immediate;
without a dependent grid the trigger has no effect. These actions
still execute and have issue/done events.
verb.store:
Walk this shard's output units and submit Y's zero stores. Done
means the local store loop finished issuing its writes; global
output visibility is guaranteed by verify.kernel_done.
verb.scan:
Initialize one DirtyLane accumulator per thread and walk the
payload, activation-scale, score and expert-parameter streams in
that order, using zero_verify's predicates. Every thread joins
the CTA predicate OR, including those with no elements to read;
its result is DirtyPart. Done covers all shard reads and this OR.
verb.publish:
The elected thread contributes a dirty bit atomically if DirtyPart
is nonzero, orders that contribution before one global arrival
ticket, then takes the ticket. The last arriving CTA reads the
combined dirty state, writes Clean and resets both counters.
It then orders these state writes before publishing the same
verdict to the pinned host mirror. Other CTAs finish after their
own contribution without waiting for the last arrival. Done
covers this CTA's state updates; neither an individual done nor
host observation of the mirror replaces verify.kernel_done for
output visibility. Same-stream execution orders subsequent device
accesses to the flag and counters; no cross-stream synchronization
is added.

verb.enter: All threads wait for predecessor-grid completion and visibility; warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. The permission does not publish Clean or the output.
verb.zero: Initialize each thread's DirtyLane word to zero. Each thread walks its positions in the assigned output stripe, writing eight BF16 zeros per position to ZeroOutput. Done covers store submission, not global visibility.
verb.compute: Visit the assigned payload, activation-scale, score and expert-parameter stripe positions in that order. Accumulate the verify_zero predicates into DirtyLane, with no early termination; optional clamp reads occur only when HasLimit=1. The output and input traversals have independent lengths. No route IDs or GEMM weight payloads/scales are accessed.
verb.publish: Rendezvous all eight warps with a CTA-wide Boolean OR of DirtyLane, producing DirtyPart. One thread per CTA atomically ORs a dirty contribution into the global sticky aggregate when needed, establishes device visibility, then obtains an arrival ticket. Only the final arrival reads the aggregate, publishes Clean and resets aggregate and ticket to zero. Other CTAs perform no publication of Clean and do not wait for the last CTA. The pinned host mirror is absent in this node. This action completes after this CTA's contribution and any elected publication/reset; verify.kernel_done covers all contributions, output stores and the verdict. DirtyLane is dead after the reduction; the global protocol state is reused only after the ordered execution completes.

verb.enter: All threads wait for predecessor-grid completion and visibility; warp 0 grants dependent-grid launch permission. Then all threads perform the guard's completion wait and read Clean before any payload, scratch or output access. The launch permission is not data readiness. Clean=1 leaves the computational work domain empty but retains this entry and kernel completion; Clean=0 proceeds with its assigned work.
verb.produce: Stage every route ID once into StagedIds and zero the full GroupTable, including the unused expert columns. After CTA rendezvous, warp g forms Hist(g) for its contiguous route group. Rendezvous before expert-wise prefixing replaces Hist with RankCursor, the group-exclusive reservation bases of routing, and writes Counts. Another rendezvous precedes the paired expert scans; ScanScratch holds two 64-word scan arrays and J. Publish Offs and TilePrefix both globally and into their local caches, then rendezvous before scatter and tile enumeration. Each warp advances its own RankCursor by atomics while writing RoutePos and all three packed maps. Enumerate and store TileExpert and TileRow from the cached tile prefix. StagedIds and the prefix caches survive through their last reads; GroupTable is overwritten only after histogram production is complete. M=0 still writes zero Counts/prefixes and RoutePos=-1, with no packed or tile stores.

verb.enter: All threads first wait for predecessor-grid completion and read Clean. Clean=1 performs no explicit dependent-grid trigger, route-table read, local initialization or allocation; this grid grants launch permission on kernel completion. Clean=0 executes the ordinary PDL wait/trigger pair, then reads J. For dirty J=0, all work domains are empty and no local allocation occurs. Otherwise warp 0 initializes the completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage, and all seven warps rendezvous once before their independent loops, including workers with no assigned item.
verb.prime: Resolve the worktile's expert, row base and reduction-slice origin. PackedToken selects hidden_states_scale rows. Load the slice's first stage and, when its stage count exceeds one, the second into APrefetch. Load only rows below valid(j); other register and shared scale rows are not initialized. Prefetch registers restart per worktile.
verb.publish: Scatter only valid rows of the current APrefetch set into AScale and establish shared-to-async visibility. If a next stage exists in this slice, load it into the other register set before the warp rendezvous and full-stage arrival. Stage 1 is loaded again after priming; that first primed copy is overwritten without use. Padding rows of AScale retain their old bytes. Done includes the arrival, not the independent payload/weight-scale transfers.
verb.retire: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For Jrun=0 this action is a no-op without resource or barrier access. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or new global fence; kernel completion supplies external visibility.

enter.meaning: All threads first wait for predecessor-grid completion and read Clean. Clean=1 performs no explicit dependent-grid trigger, route-table read, local initialization or allocation; this grid grants launch permission on kernel completion. Clean=0 executes the ordinary PDL wait/trigger pair, then reads J. For dirty J=0, all work domains are empty and no local allocation occurs. Otherwise warp 0 initializes the completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage, and all seven warps rendezvous once before their independent loops, including workers with no assigned item.

verb.load: Using PackedToken, issue ceil_div(valid(j),4) four-row gathers from hidden_states into PayloadA and two contiguous up/gate weight boxes into PayloadB, at this slice's channel offset. In the last partial four-row group, extra payload rows repeat the first valid token; later groups are not fetched or initialized. Arm the full-stage transaction count for (2*BN1+4*ceil_div(valid(j),4))*(BK/2) bytes. Done covers all these payload transfers; payload slots remain independent of scale-slot reuse.
verb.stage: Copy prepared weight scales into BScale's fused 128-row up/gate image, preserving the prepared ABI permutation. The lane-permuted 4-byte asynchronous copies collectively stage 2048 bytes. Done is their completion arrival to the full-stage protocol. Also issue an L2-only weight-scale hint two stages ahead when that stage lies in the same worktile; the hint has no consumer or completion edge.

retire.meaning: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For Jrun=0 this action is a no-op without resource or barrier access. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or new global fence; kernel completion supplies external visibility.

enter.meaning: All threads first wait for predecessor-grid completion and read Clean. Clean=1 performs no explicit dependent-grid trigger, route-table read, local initialization or allocation; this grid grants launch permission on kernel completion. Clean=0 executes the ordinary PDL wait/trigger pair, then reads J. For dirty J=0, all work domains are empty and no local allocation occurs. Otherwise warp 0 initializes the completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage, and all seven warps rendezvous once before their independent loops, including workers with no assigned item.

wait.meaning: Drain(t,q) completes after the four explicit prior-work accumulator releases. q identifies the one noninitial-work wait; FC1 performs this wait before its first scale copy.

verb.prepare: The elected issuer waits for the full-stage protocol and copies AScale and BScale into ScaleTM: four scale-copy operations for each operand. Issuance includes submission of all scale copies; only then does this issuer advance to the MMA action. Done is covered by the following cumulative MMA completion.
verb.mma: Consume PayloadA/PayloadB and ScaleTM in four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates to C1. The first update initializes C1 without reading its old value. The fused 128-column product covers both up and gate. Issue a cumulative completion commit after each stage; done covers scale copies, payload reads and accumulator updates. The last stage also commits result readiness for the epilogue. Same-issuer ordering ensures an earlier MMA has consumed ScaleTM before a later scale copy overwrites that scale slot, and makes each scale copy visible before the MMA that uses it.

retire.meaning: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For Jrun=0 this action is a no-op without resource or barrier access. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or new global fence; kernel completion supplies external visibility.

verb.enter: All threads first wait for predecessor-grid completion and read Clean. Clean=1 performs no explicit dependent-grid trigger, route-table read, local initialization or allocation; this grid grants launch permission on kernel completion. Clean=0 executes the ordinary PDL wait/trigger pair, then reads J. For dirty J=0, all work domains are empty and no local allocation occurs. Otherwise warp 0 initializes the completion protocol and allocates TensorStorage, and all seven warps rendezvous once before their independent loops, including workers with no assigned item.
verb.drain: Each warp owns its hardware TMEM quadrant (warp index modulo four), one row per lane. For c=0 or 1, load the matching 32 up and 32 gate values into this quadrant's rows of Fragment, issue both reads before waiting, and wait for all their TMEM reads to retire. Done makes this register fragment usable.
verb.emit: Store the 32 up and 32 gate FP32 Fragment values directly into the matching Part slice for valid rows. Padding rows perform the reads but no stores. Done means store submission has consumed Fragment; global stores may still be in flight.
verb.release: After both chunks have been drained and their raw partial stores submitted, rendezvous this warp and arrive once to release its accumulator quadrant. Next-work scale preparation waits for all four epilogue roles; global partial-store completion is provided by kernel completion.
verb.retire: After this role's whole assigned sequence, rendezvous with all seven warps; warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For Jrun=0 this action is a no-op without resource or barrier access. It does not insert a per-worktile drain or new global fence; kernel completion supplies external visibility.

verb.enter: All threads first wait for predecessor-grid completion and read Clean. Clean=1 performs no explicit dependent-grid trigger, route-table read, local initialization or allocation; this grid grants launch permission on kernel completion. Clean=0 executes the ordinary PDL wait/trigger pair, then reads J. For dirty J=0, all work domains are empty and no local allocation occurs. For every in-range backing row, load both slice vectors into PartialLoad before the expert-ID test. Out-of-range packet lanes do no reads; unused route rows still load allocated backing bytes. verb.produce: Read PackedExpert's backing row and reject out-of-range IDs before any per-expert parameter access. Accepted groups merge the retained slices into Merged in ascending order, then compute merge_quantize into Activated. Four-lane maximum exchange combines all 16 absolute values; paired neighbor exchange assembles packed payload words. Store ActQ and one ActS byte per accepted block, including unused backing rows that pass the check. No cross-block or cross-CTA exchange is needed. Rejected groups perform no arithmetic or stores, but the action still completes. PartialLoad is dead after the merge; Merged is dead after activation; Activated is dead after quantization and store submission.

verb.compute: Rows(t) resolves the worktile expert and base(j), then fills RowIndex[r] with base(j)+r for r<valid(j) and base(j) otherwise. All four warps rendezvous before using it for scale loads. RowIndex survives through this worktile's scale staging; payload boxes use consecutive rows directly and do not use RowIndex.

stage.meaning: Future(t,q) always commits one asynchronous-copy group. For q<I/BK, issue four 4-byte copies per row for each scale operand into AScale and BScale. RowIndex selects ActS rows; prepared weight-scale addressing preserves the Contract permutation. One elected thread issues the consecutive ActQ box and prepared-weight box into PayloadA and PayloadB, with a joint payload transaction count of (BM+BN2)*(BK/2) bytes. All four objects use slot g[t,q]%3. Done covers both payload transactions and the scale copies, which have distinct completion mechanisms. For q>=I/BK there are no data transfers or resource accesses, but the empty group commit and its events remain. The two leading groups precede the main loop; each iteration then issues the group two stages ahead, so the wait with two newer groups outstanding retires the current scale group even at the tail. There is no register scale-prefetch slab.

verb.wait: Prior(t,i,u) waits for the explicit previous-stage MMA completion and rendezvous of all four warps; u names its noninitial-stage occurrence. Stage(g) waits for that stage's scale-copy group and payload-byte completion, then rendezvous and establish visibility to the tensor operation. Result(t) waits for the last MMA commit and rendezvous before any accumulator reads. These waits preserve carried completion parity; none is an early dependent-grid launch permission.

contract.meaning: For C2(g), the elected warp-0 issuer copies AScale and BScale into ScaleTM, then issues the four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of fc2. The first update of each worktile initializes C2 without reading old accumulator data. Commit one cumulative completion covering scale copies, payload reads and accumulator writes. Same-issuer ordering makes the scale copies visible to their MMA consumers. No other warp is an independent producer or epilogue role.

verb.release: Worktile(t) rendezvous all four warps after all fragment reads and direct-store submissions. This permits the next worktile to overwrite C2, RowIndex and operand slots; no next-work prime is issued before this point. Global stores may remain in flight.
verb.retire: After the whole assigned sequence, warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For Jrun=0 this is a no-op without resource or barrier access; for dirty J>0 an empty worker still retires its allocation. All MMA and TMEM reads have retired, and every issued data-copy group has been consumed. Kernel completion covers direct global stores; empty copy-group commits need no payload drain.
verb.produce: For RouteResult(t), each warp independently walks BN2/32 consecutive 32-column chunks. Read its hardware quadrant, one row per lane, into Fragment and wait for those TMEM reads to retire. Read all BM rows, including padding; convert to BF16 with round-to-nearest-even and directly store only rows r<valid(j). The next chunk reuses that warp's Fragment after store submission has consumed it. Warps need no rendezvous between chunks. Done covers all chunk reads, conversions and store submissions, with global visibility supplied by kernel completion. No shared output sink or bulk output store is used.

verb.publish: The elected thread contributes a dirty bit with global atomic OR when needed, establishes global ordering, then atomically increments the arrival counter. The last arrival reads the combined dirty word, writes Clean, and resets dirty and arrival words to zero. If HostMirror=1 it establishes system visibility before writing CleanMirror; nonlast workers do not write either final verdict. The saved int32[4] zflag workspace holds Clean, dirty, arrival and one unused word. Publication initially zeroes it; later invocations reuse the last-arrival reset only after prior guards have finished. No worker spins waiting for other verifier CTAs. This action completes each worker's contribution; verify.kernel_done, not one worker's done or launch_ready, exposes the complete output and verdict.

verb.compute: Initialize one DirtyVote per participating thread to zero, then scan its assigned payload, activation-scale, score and parameter chunks in separate loops using verify_zero predicates. Accumulate dirty bits without early termination. No route ID, weight payload or weight scale is read.
verb.publish: The retained global ABI state has four int32 words: verdict, dirty OR, arrivals and one unused reserved word. Dirty OR and arrivals start at zero from ABI construction or the preceding completed verification. Reduce DirtyVote with a CTA-wide Boolean OR. A dirty member atomically ORs one into the retained global dirty word. Its elected thread makes that update visible before taking one atomic arrival ticket; clean members also take a ticket. The last member reads the aggregate, stores ZeroClean and resets dirty and arrivals to zero. Nonlast members finish after their arrival; last-member completion includes verdict publication and reset. Consumers wait for full kernel completion, not merely the ticket or launch permission. There is no host-mirror write.

Another rendezvous precedes the paired expert scans; ScanScratch holds two 64-word scan arrays and J. Publish Offs and TilePrefix both globally and into their local caches, then rendezvous before scatter and tile enumeration. Each warp advances its own RankCursor by atomics while writing RoutePos and all three packed maps. Enumerate and store TileExpert and TileRow from the cached tile prefix. StagedIds and the prefix caches survive through their last reads; GroupTable is overwritten only after histogram production is complete. M=0 still writes zero Counts/prefixes and RoutePos=-1, with no packed or tile stores.

wait.meaning: Drain(t,q) completes after the four explicit prior-work accumulator releases. q identifies the one noninitial-work wait, before the first scale copy.

verb.prepare: The elected issuer waits for the full-stage protocol and copies AScale and BScale into ScaleTM: four scale-copy operations for each operand. Issuance includes submission of all scale copies; only then does this issuer advance to the MMA action. Done is covered by the following cumulative MMA completion.
verb.mma: Execute four ordered 64-channel block-scaled updates of C2, with first-update initialization and cumulative stage completion. Done covers preceding scale copies and operand reads; last-stage commit also publishes the result. Same-issuer scale-copy/MMA ordering protects ScaleTM reuse and copy-to-MMA visibility.

retire.meaning: After this role's assigned sequence, all seven warps rendezvous and warp 0 deallocates TensorStorage. For Active=0 or J=0 this declared action is a no-op with issue/done. There is no per-worktile drain or extra global fence; kernel completion supplies external store visibility.

guard.meaning: Wait for full predecessor-grid completion and visibility, then read the current global ZeroClean. Done records the uniform clean/dirty decision for this CTA. Clean has no subsequent full-chain data accesses; the submitted kernel and its completion event remain.

verb.enter: On Active=0 this post-guard entry is a no-op: no trigger, routing-scratch read, rendezvous or TMEM allocation occurs; launch_ready is supplied by kernel completion. Even workers with no assigned item participate in this initialization.
verb.drain: Each warp owns its hardware TMEM quadrant (warp index modulo four), one row per lane. Read the single 32-column chunk c into that quadrant's rows of Fragment and wait for its TMEM reads to retire. Padding rows are read too; done makes Fragment usable.
verb.release: After all four chunks have been drained and their direct stores submitted, rendezvous this warp and arrive once to release its accumulator quadrant. Next-work scale preparation waits for all four epilogue roles; kernel completion supplies global store visibility.
verb.emit: For valid rows, convert Fragment to BF16 and submit direct stores into the matching 32-column RouteResult region. Padding rows perform no conversion or stores. Done means store submission has consumed Fragment; global stores may still be in flight.
